fullText:
Microsoft co-founder and philanthropist speaks with NBC’s Kristen Welker in interview airing on Sunday

Bill Gates has called on the US’s federal legislators and law enforcers to regulate the development of artificial intelligence (AI), saying in an interview airing on Sunday that the technology left unchecked could cause “a billion deaths” and “no one thinks self-regulation is enough”.

“You need law enforcement and the politicians to get into the discussion about what safeguards and monitoring look like,” the Microsoft co-founder and philanthropist said to Kristen Welker, the NBC Meet the Press host. “And that has to be a required thing.”

Using a term meant to describe an expense required to run a business, Gates continued: “It will be a little bit of overhead for the industry – but not a dramatic slowing of what they’re doing.”

Another portion of the interview – excerpts of which NBC circulated in advance – saw Gates dramatically warn that AI in the wrong hands would be “certainly powerful enough to drive events that, you know, cause a billion deaths”.

“There’s never been a weapon as powerful as the combination of people with ill intent using the latest AI tools,” Gates added, echoing other recent similar warnings by a wide array of tech and political figures.

Gates also addressed the concept of a “kill switch” that could turn off AI if it became too potent, saying it was inadequate.

“It’s not enough to have a kill switch,” Gates remarked. “We’re not yet at the point where … they autonomously grab computers and, you know, can’t be shut down. So that discussion … just sort of shows how non-technical various people are.”

Gates otherwise is generally regarded as optimistic about humans’ future. Many reporting or commenting on his conversation with Welker noted that it occurred in the wake of a nearly 6,000-word essay that he published in late August warning about AI and the potentially lethal ills it poses to humanity on a large scale.

His fellow tech moguls including Sam Altman and Elon Musk have joined Gates in calling for a slowdown of the development of AI, which some experts theorize could precipitate the mass destruction of humans through bioweapons and nuclear war, among other methods.

Progressive US senator Bernie Sanders on 23 September proposed legislation that would temporarily pause advanced AI development while guardrails to the technology are put in place.

Meanwhile, Microsoft itself has been challenged for having a role in stoking some of the dystopian concerns surrounding AI.

Company employees and activists have organized a campaign aimed at getting Microsoft to cut ties with the Israeli military, which has used AI tools to kill in Gaza and – alongside US forces – in Iran, according to a Guardian essay published on Friday.

The essay’s authors, Mohamed Hussein and Granate Kim of the No Azure for Apartheid group, furthermore warned that “horrors wrought by AI” are also being seen in the US. For instance, the US Department of Homeland Security has used AI tools such as Microsoft’s Azure to monitor, arrest and deport immigrants en masse, Hussein and Kim wrote.

Gates’s essay in August and interview on Sunday were two of his first major forays into the public since becoming ensnared in the scandal surrounding Jeffrey Epstein, the disgraced financier who pleaded guilty in 2008 to procuring a minor for prostitution before dying by suicide while incarcerated on sex-trafficking charges 11 years later.

An external review commissioned by Gates’s philanthropic foundation and released in July determined that he was among a number of organization staffers and leaders who had collectively held about 30 meetings with Epstein from 2011 to 2014.

Gates has not been accused of involvement in Epstein’s admitted or alleged crimes. He has said he regretted “every minute” he spent with Epstein, and remains the chair of the $89bn (£65bn) Gates Foundation charity.

In a lighter moment during Welker’s interview with Gates, the host asked him: “Are there any ways in which you, professionally or personally, avoid AI and say that: ‘I’m not going to consult with it in this instance?’”

Gates, with a chuckle and a smile, replied: “Well, I’m not using it for my personal relationships. I’m not like: ‘Hey, do you like me? Hey, am I a nice guy?’

“So I just never went down that path, because I’m lucky in terms of my family, friends and everything. I don’t socialize with the AI. It knows I’m a very serious person.”

title: Democracy blindsides Silicon Valley’s power players looking to transform the world with AI
description:
‘The push against datacenters speaks to the frustration of people who don’t feel they are making the choices in their lives’
The Stanford ethicist Rob Reich was once invited to a dinner organized by a Silicon Valley mogul to discuss what a state designed to maximize science and tech powered by commercial models might look like. The gathered technologists were drawn to the idea of building a small nation-state dedicated to the endeavor, Reich recalls in “System Error: Where Big Tech Went Wrong and How We Can Reboot it”.
When Reich asked whether this state would be a democracy, he got a cool no. “Democracy is too slow, and it holds science back,” he was told. “To optimize for science, we need a beneficent technocrat in charge.
fullText:
The Stanford ethicist Rob Reich was once invited to a dinner organized by a Silicon Valley mogul to discuss what a state designed to maximize science and tech powered by commercial models might look like. The gathered technologists were drawn to the idea of building a small nation-state dedicated to the endeavor, Reich recalls in “System Error: Where Big Tech Went Wrong and How We Can Reboot it”.

When Reich asked whether this state would be a democracy, he got a cool no. “Democracy is too slow, and it holds science back,” he was told. “To optimize for science, we need a beneficent technocrat in charge.”

The technos were onto something. Silicon Valley’s power players have just been blindsided by democracy, which has slammed into their program to transform the world with artificial intelligence. A cabal that never doubted the greatness of their ambitions unexpectedly finds their project in the hot seat, forcing them into the unusual position of having to persuade the great unwashed of the merits of their endeavor. So far, the public is not buying. And for all their blindingly high IQs and their massively endowed wallets, Silicon Valley’s greats don’t quite know what to do.

Everyday Americans are up in arms against the AI datacenters sprouting across their communities. Villages, counties, cities and states are imposing moratoria and bans on further development. While the backlash has largely focused on stopping the proliferation of sprawling sites packed with energy-guzzling computer servers, the revolt is not merely nimby opposition to local development.

Public opinion has also turned decidedly sour on the AI project that has called these datacenters into being. Some 73% of Americans think the costs of datacenters outweigh the benefits, according to a survey by the Marquette University Law School. The same survey found that 70% of Americans think that AI is bad for society.

Americans were not always this down on the tech. In 2021, only 37% declared themselves more concerned than excited about the technology, according to surveys by the Pew Research Center. But the share has climbed to 52%. Even 55% of young adults – usually the most excited cohort – have soured on it. And this is not a partisan fear. Democrats and Republicans alike are vastly more concerned than excited. Interestingly, Americans are generally more mistrustful of the technology than people in other countries.

This surely has something to do with the terrifying announcements that have come out of Silicon Valley recently. A widely shared belief that there’s at least a 10% chance that AI could cause human extinction has, rightly, scared the bejesus out of many and follows repeated statements that artificial intelligence will end all jobs as we know them. Assuming we do avoid an AI apocalypse, vague promises of an AI cure for cancer and a universal basic income or some such to replace wages across the economy sound hollow coming from a clutch of out-of-touch billionaires with questionable moral codes in a country with huge holes in its social safety net.

The political backlash is built on a deeper discomfort, though, beyond fear of the dystopia threatened by the masters of the valley. A fear built in the here and now and fueled by a brooding mistrust in US democracy itself, distrust of a political system that allowed a clutch of weird, sci-fi addled plutocrats to pursue a civilization-threatening project behind people’s backs. As noted Henry Farrell, a political scientist at Johns Hopkins University, “the push against datacenters speaks to the frustration of people who don’t feel they are making the choices in their lives.”

People are not wrong about this. As AI ethicist Rumman Chowdhury points out, the dominant narrative out of Silicon Valley, that AI systems are becoming so powerful that nobody – including the companies that developed them – can stop them, is a stratagem to avoid responsibility for whatever harm their products may cause, depriving meat-and-bones humans of any recourse to law.

The popular backlash is unlikely to stop the buildout of datacenters. Donald Trump remains steadfastly on the side of the moguls hoping to build an AI future. In response to the popular backlash, the Environmental Protection Agency is planning to nix the rule that requires states to solicit public input on applications for air pollution permits for industrial facilities like datacenters and the power plants that feed them, which could keep locals in the dark until construction starts.

The sorry truth is that tech’s power does insulate it from small democratic pressure. “If there is one sector in the US that is still globally dominant and profitable, it is tech,” Boston University historian Quinn Slobodian said. “They can be confident that even if there is a change of leadership, the next person will have to dance with them anyway.”

Critically, there is a bipartisan consensus that ensuring the US’s capabilities in artificial intelligence remain ahead of China’s is of paramount importance. Fear of Chinese catch-up is likely to keep driving policy, overriding voters’ concerns about the risks embodied in this new technology.

And yet voters’ rejection of datacenters, the most immediate, concrete expression of the AI project, raises a question about how the technological revolution of our time will deal with intense popular skepticism and navigate democratic governance. It poses a challenge to a technological elite which exhibits nothing but contempt toward democratic rule.

This is not, of course, the first time that some technological revolution brings about societal upheaval without asking for democratic buy-in. The people that brought about America’s transformation from an agricultural society to an industrial powerhouse did not survey farmers about what mechanization would do to their farms. The Luddites of 19th century England would have loved the chance to put approval of the steam-powered loom to a referendum.

But technological change over the last few decades has not delivered the kind of uplift to everyday workers that their ancestors enjoyed as they were displaced from agriculture to join a highly productive industrial labor force. Automation, instead, has flushed workers without a college degree into a low productivity economy where hotel and restaurant workers, nursing home caretakers, janitors and 7-11 cashiers eke out a living on little more than the minimum wage. Americans have earned their skepticism about the wonders of AI.

One must wonder how such a transformative project as the mass deployment of artificial intelligence across society and the economy will navigate today’s democratic political systems. The technological elite’s contempt for the people’s concerns suggests that they hope to somehow bypass popular concerns in pursuit of the AI program. It seems unlikely that a crew of billionaires who dream of building enclaves at sea, outside the legal jurisdiction of any state, will simply accept democratic constraints. The question is what they will do to overcome them.

Until China became a hi-tech powerhouse and proved them wrong, the political class across the liberal market democracies of the West was convinced that capitalism needed democracy to thrive. But the neoliberal project that guided policy across much of the 20th century was largely about putting capitalism beyond democracy’s reach.

The emergence of independent central banks like the Federal Reserve, which is supposed to set interest rates free from political pressure, is perhaps the prime example of this process. The agreements that led to the creation of the World Trade Organization were largely about putting trade policy beyond the reach of domestic politics. Myriad international treaties were similarly designed to protect economic intercourse from democratic challenges, to provide businesses insulation from political agendas and guarantee the political stability they required to invest.

But the neoliberal project was not driven by “a foundational belief that democracy needs to be snuffed out entirely,” noted Slobodian, author of “Globalists” which traces the history of neoliberalism, as well as an explanatory tome on Elon Musk, “Muskism: A Guide for the Perplexed.” It “acknowledged at some basic level the legitimacy of democracy, which needs to be counterbalanced.”

The barons of Silicon Valley are not so forgiving. “The Silicon Valley leadership class has a programmers’ mentality,” said Slobodian. “For them, the messiness of democracy has no function or utility. It is only bad code.”

Peter Thiel, the weirdest of the Silicon Valley billionaires, who can’t but bring up the Antichrist in every conversation, has argued that democracy and liberty are incompatible. Similar strains of thought are also popular with the less idiosyncratic billionaires in the Valley ecosystem. OpenAI’s Sam Altman salivates about an “awesome” future in which human presidents are replaced with an AI that “can go around and talk to every person on Earth, understand their exact preferences at a very deep level, you know, how they think about this issue and that one and how they balance the trade-offs and what they want and then understand all of that and like collectively optimize for the collective preferences of humanity or of citizens of the US.”

The technos’ conflict is not exclusively with democracy. It is with any institution that dares impose constraints on whatever Grand Project they plan to unleash on the world. This could be reconfiguring human interactions by plugging everybody into social media, inventing a new form of money that can evade government control, civilizing space or bringing about a superintelligent Golem.

Musk has no patience for corporate governance tools that may limit what he can do at the helm of his empire. He aspires to be answerable to no one and will organize his companies to that effect. Thiel can’t even countenance competition. It “means no profits for anybody, no meaningful differentiation, and a struggle for survival,” he has fumed. Across the Valley, these thoughts draw from an unshakeable faith in the civilizational, transformative greatness of their endeavor. Technology will solve the world. They will provide the technology. Everybody else, please get out of the way.

There is, however, a historical discontinuity to the story of these masters of the universe: They used to think of themselves as the Good Guys in the liberal democratic fold. Most of them were aligned with the Democratic Party, culturally liberal, empathetic, and willing to accept some modicum of taxation to finance redistribution. Emerging after the collapse of the Soviet block and the end of the Cold War, they saw themselves and their companies as agents of the End of History in Francis Fukuyama’s sense of the word.

Social media–Silicon Valley’s original Grand Project– would overcome the censorship and limits to expression that underpin authoritarian rule, unshackling freedom of expression and opening the floodgates for liberty and democracy. The project sounded so good that the masters of the Valley managed to convince Congress in 1996 to give them a free pass: section 230 of the Telecommunications Act, which said social media companies were not responsible for anything posted on their platforms, based on the dubious argument that they just provided the blackboard but had no say over what was written on it.

Then, the tech moguls’ love affair with democracy went sour. For it turned out that social media could also do a lot of damage. Reports of teen suicides and online bullying bred unease about social media, which built into open mistrust as it became evident that the billionaires at the helm of these technologies knew about the potential perils of their products and yet kept adding features designed to hook users to their screens.

When social media platforms emerged as vectors of misinformation and political manipulation during the 2016 election, the romance between the tech bros and society fractured irretrievably. Founders and their funders who were used to being revered as purveyors of rainbows and puppies, found themselves under harshly unsympathetic scrutiny.

How long will the honeymoon last? Mark Zuckerberg seems excited about the gold chains, the new hairdo and the mixed martial arts. Perhaps his embrace of the Maga-friendly manosphere is genuine. Musk, Jeff Bezos, Peter Thiel, Altman all seem comfy in Trump’s squishy embrace. And Trump’s Washington keeps giving Silicon Valley what it wants. The administration is promising to punish European countries who dare fine the US’s hi-tech behemoths. The president has called the power plants built to feed AI datacenters “beautiful”. And he will never do anything to hinder crypto, which is proving so lucrative for him and his family.

Still, the furious backlash against datacenters suggests that Silicon Valley’s Maga-friendly strategy may run out of runway. Their allegiance with Trump, whose popularity ratings are plummeting, may start feeling like an anvil around their neck.

Abdul El-Sayed, the democratic socialist running for the Senate in Michigan, put it this way in a conversation with Jasmine Sun: “This entire industry feels misplaced, and it’s being driven by the interaction between all the worst players. Number one, tech billionaires who are already billionaires, who don’t really need more money but want power. And then VC firms who want to make more money. And then big corporations who want to automate your job. So who wins here? Definitely not the people who live there.”

Silicon Valley may have oodles of money to change the conversation. But it is right to be terrified that this argument may win the day. As Slobodian put it, “the tech barons may not care about democracy, but democracy cares about them.”

Eduardo Porter is a journalist focused on economics and politics. He writes the newsletter Being There on Substack

fullText:
TAIPEI, Sept 27 (Reuters) - The United States "very much" understands Taiwan's defence needs and the severe military threat it faces from China, a senior ‌Taiwanese diplomat said on Sunday, following a Washington summit between the US ‌and Chinese leaders.

Democratically governed Taiwan, which China claims as its own territory, has been waiting for months ​for US President Donald Trump to approve a new arms sales package worth some $14 billion, following up on a record $11 billion deal unveiled last December.

After meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing in May, Trump said he was keeping the latest arms ‌sales package in abeyance. Trump ⁠has not mentioned the sale since last week's summit, saying only on Saturday that Xi understands his position on Taiwan.

Speaking to ⁠reporters in Taipei, Taiwan Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi pointed to comments by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio that military sales to anyone require the same careful consideration.

"Taiwan ​faces a ​severe situation in the Taiwan Strait. Even ​though China's economy is declining, ‌it continues investing more resources into building military capacity. Under this context, the US very much understands our defence needs," he said.

Washington also understands Taiwan's determination to invest in its military, Chen added.

"We do continuously communicate with them, and we believe the US understands the situation we face and our determination on defence investment completely."

The ‌United States is bound by law to provide ​Taiwan with the means to defend itself. China ​has repeatedly called for military ​sales to end.

David Perdue, the US ambassador to China, told CNBC ‌on Friday that there has been ​no change in Taiwan ​policy by Trump, including on arms sales.

Chen said Taiwan had received confirmation "from our American friends repeatedly that US policy toward Taiwan remains unchanged".

Taiwan's government ​rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims, saying ‌only the island's people can decide their future.

China has rebuffed repeated calls ​for talks by Taiwan President Lai Ching-te, whom it calls a "separatist".

(Reporting ​by Ben Blanchard; Editing by Jamie Freed)

title: Two giant pandas sent by China arrive in Atlanta on 10-year loan
description:
A panda at the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding, where the pair sent to Atlanta departed from (Hector RETAMAL)
Two giant pandas sent by China arrived in the United States on Sunday, Beijing's state media said, after a leaders' summit that was heavy on symbolism and light on major breakthroughs.
The pandas' transfer had already been agreed but the departure was announced Thursday during Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington.
The black-and-white mammals are immensely popular around the world, and China loans them out as part of a "panda diplomacy" programme to foster foreign ties.
Ping Ping and Fu Shuang departed from Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport on a chartered flight at around 3:00 am (1900 GMT on Saturday), state news agency Xinhua reported.
After a 16-hour flight that crossed the international date line, the bears touched down in Atlanta, Georgia shortly before 7:00 am local time (1100 GMT on Sunday), Xinhua said later.

The black-and-white mammals are immensely popular around the world, and China loans them out as part of a "panda diplomacy" programme to foster foreign ties.

Ping Ping and Fu Shuang departed from Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport on a chartered flight at around 3:00 am (1900 GMT on Saturday), state news agency Xinhua reported.

After a 16-hour flight that crossed the international date line, the bears touched down in Atlanta, Georgia shortly before 7:00 am local time (1100 GMT on Sunday), Xinhua said later.

Steamed corn buns, bamboo shoots and carrots were prepared to keep the pandas nourished during their flight, Chinese state-run media the Global Times reported.

The Boeing 777 operated by FedEx was the top-tracked aircraft on aviation information platform FlightRadar24 as it neared Alaska, roughly halfway into its journey.

The pandas will be hosted by Zoo Atlanta for the next 10 years.

A farewell ceremony was held for the pair before their departure by the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding.

Experienced keepers were dispatched by the US side to accompany the duo on their flight, the Global Times reported.

In preparation for their arrival, Zoo Atlanta has renovated its panda facilities and assembled a team of animal caretakers.

It has also ensured a stable and long-term supply of bamboo, grown locally in Atlanta, which has a climate that is very similar to Chengdu.

Zoo Atlanta previously hosted pandas on loan from China for a quarter of a century starting in 1999, but it has not had any since 2024.

Both arrivals were born in 2020. Ping Ping, a male, is now six years old while Fu Shuang, a female, will turn six next month.

Pandas in captivity typically live for around 30 years.

Beijing has sent the furry creatures across the globe for decades as soft-power ambassadors of its diplomatic goodwill.

In 1972, China gifted a pair of pandas to Washington, following US president Richard Nixon's historic visit to the Communist nation.

Beijing recalled two of its pandas from Japan early this year, following a diplomatic spat that began when Japan's prime minister hinted that Tokyo could intervene militarily in the event of any attack on Taiwan.

title: Nor'easter floods the coast, leaving 1 man dead and thousands without power
description:
A slow-moving nor'easter continued to batter the Northeast on Sunday, bringing more rain, strong winds and another round of coastal flooding after a weekend that killed at least one person.
A New York City Housing Authority employee died Saturday afternoon after a tree fell on him in East New York, Brooklyn, CBS News reported. A man who had been reported missing after he was seen swimming off Fire Island on Saturday contacted police Sunday morning and was found unharmed, state police said.
About 136,000 homes and businesses were without power across New Jersey, New York, Connecticut, Massachusetts and Rhode Island as of Sunday morning, according to PowerOutage.us, up from about 85,000 on Saturday.
fullText:
A slow-moving nor'easter continued to batter the Northeast on Sunday, bringing more rain, strong winds and another round of coastal flooding after a weekend that killed at least one person.

A New York City Housing Authority employee died Saturday afternoon after a tree fell on him in East New York, Brooklyn, CBS News reported. A man who had been reported missing after he was seen swimming off Fire Island on Saturday contacted police Sunday morning and was found unharmed, state police said.

About 136,000 homes and businesses were without power across New Jersey, New York, Connecticut, Massachusetts and Rhode Island as of Sunday morning, according to PowerOutage.us, up from about 85,000 on Saturday. Ocean and Monmouth counties in New Jersey and Suffolk County on Long Island were among the hardest hit.

The storm was drifting near the New Jersey coast Sunday morning and is expected to ease Sunday afternoon before moving away late Monday, according to the National Weather Service. Minor to moderate coastal flooding was expected with Sunday morning's high tide, and gusts of 40 to 50 mph remained possible from New Jersey to Long Island. More than 6 inches of rain had fallen in parts of southeastern Massachusetts and about 5 inches along the northern Jersey Shore.

Never drive or walk through floodwaters. Just 6 inches of moving water can knock a person down.

Move cars out of flood-prone areas before high tide.

If you live in a basement or ground-floor apartment, have more than one way out.

Stay away from downed power lines and report them to your utility or 911.

In New York City, text NOTIFYNYC to 692-692 for emergency alerts.

Follow below for the latest updates.

People in flooded coastal neighborhoods of New York and New Jersey took to kayaks and canoes over the weekend, paddling down streets past cars sitting in deep water, CBS News reported.

In Howard Beach, Queens, water ranged from several inches to more than a foot deep Saturday, according to CBS New York. A video posted by a storm chaser that morning showed two people paddling to the entrance of the Howard Beach–JFK Airport station, and it had drawn millions of views on X.

Water at Kings Point, N.Y., on western Long Island Sound, reached about 3 feet above the normal high-tide mark just after 11 a.m. Sunday and was still rising, according to preliminary NOAA data. That's already higher than the gauge reached with Saturday night's tide.

NYC Emergency Management had warned that the midday tide could bring moderate flooding to the coastal Bronx and northern Queens, including parts of Flushing and Astoria.

The hurricane watch and tropical storm warning for Hawaii's Big Island have been lifted, and there are no coastal watches or warnings in effect for the islands, according to the Central Pacific Hurricane Center. As of 11 p.m. HST Saturday, Nolo was about 200 miles south-southwest of South Point, moving west at 9 mph with 100 mph winds. It is still expected to become a major hurricane Sunday or Sunday night but stay well south of the main islands.

Emergency crews in Sea Bright, N.J., rescued a woman and her dog after their car became trapped in floodwaters, ABC7 reported, according to the Associated Press. In Surf City, a marina owner said customers reported boats and Jet Skis missing or blown off their lifts.

Farther south, flooding cut off highway access to North Carolina's Hatteras Island, stranding visitors, the AP reported.

Water at Sandy Hook, N.J., reached about 3.3 feet above the normal high-tide mark shortly after 9 a.m. Sunday, nearly matching Saturday's peak, according to preliminary NOAA data. At the Battery in Lower Manhattan, water rose to about 2.9 feet above normal around 9:45 a.m., and Atlantic City reached about 2.8 feet.

NYC Emergency Management had warned that Sunday's midday tide could bring moderate flooding to the coastal Bronx and northern Queens, including parts of Flushing and Astoria.

Rain totals climbed overnight, with the heaviest amounts in southeastern Massachusetts and along the northern Jersey Shore, according to National Weather Service reports.

A volunteer observer north of New Bedford, Mass., measured 6.47 inches by Sunday morning, and Bridgewater, Mass., recorded more than 5 inches, according to the NWS in Boston. In New Jersey, Bradley Beach recorded about 5.1 inches and Long Branch about 4.4 inches, according to the NWS in Mount Holly. On Long Island, East Hampton and Southold recorded more than 3 inches, as did Howard Beach in Queens, the NWS in New York reported.

Up to 2 to 4 more inches are possible in parts of coastal New Jersey and New England through Monday, ABC News reported.

About 136,000 customers were without power across five Northeast states as of about 10:30 a.m. Sunday, according to PowerOutage.us, up sharply from Saturday.

New Jersey had about 57,700 outages, including more than 24,000 in Ocean County and 13,000 in Monmouth County. New York had about 36,300, with nearly 18,500 in Suffolk County. Connecticut had about 29,200 and Massachusetts about 11,300.

A 56-year-old New York City Housing Authority employee died Saturday after a tree fell on him near the Cypress Hills Houses in East New York, Brooklyn, CBS New York reported. Police said he was taken to a hospital around 3:30 p.m. and died of his injuries. CBS News identified him as Leighton Brown.

A man who had been the subject of a search after he was seen swimming in rough surf off Robert Moses State Park on Fire Island on Saturday was located alive and uninjured Sunday morning, New York State Police said. Police said the man contacted them after seeing news coverage of the search.

Most of Long Island and New York City had received 1 to 2 inches of rain by Saturday afternoon, according to National Weather Service reports. A weather station in Long Beach, N.Y., recorded 2.27 inches, one of the highest totals in the region. The NWS office in Upton, N.Y., measured 1.85 inches, and JFK Airport had 1.27 inches.

Forecasters expect the heaviest rain overnight. City officials said bands of rain falling at up to 1 inch an hour are expected from about 8 p.m. Saturday into Sunday morning, with some neighborhoods getting 2 to 3 inches more.

Emergency workers evacuated about 20 people from a waterfront Comfort Inn in Edgewater, N.J., on Saturday morning after its first floor flooded, and were going back for more, The New York Times reported.

Federal air traffic officials warned that ground stops or delays are possible Saturday evening at the three major airports serving New York City, according to an FAA advisory. Boston Logan remains the hardest hit so far, with about a quarter of its flights canceled.

Amtrak has also canceled several trains, including service between Connecticut and Massachusetts and some trains between Boston and Philadelphia, citing weather and downed wires.

Along with the Global Citizen Festival and Ed Sheeran's Gillette Stadium shows, organizers across the region have canceled or rescheduled events because of the storm:

AC/DC's Friday concert at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J., was postponed to Oct. 2, the stadium said.

All Things Go, a three-day music festival in New York City, was canceled, with refunds offered.

Saturday's Yankees-Orioles game was moved to a Friday doubleheader, and tickets can be exchanged.

An Ironman triathlon at Jones Beach was canceled.

Horse racing at Belmont Park was canceled Saturday and Sunday, the New York Racing Association said.

The New York Renaissance Faire in Tuxedo Park is closed for the weekend, with automatic refunds, organizers said.

Water levels along the New York and New Jersey coast fell well below their morning peaks by early Saturday afternoon, according to NOAA tide gauges. At the Battery in Lower Manhattan, the water dropped more than 5 feet from its 9:36 a.m. peak by just after 2 p.m.

However, the drop is temporary. The next high tide is expected around 8:15 to 9 p.m. along the city's south shore and near midnight along Long Island Sound, according to NYC Emergency Management, with moderate flooding expected again in Jamaica Bay and the Rockaways. Forecasters have said the heaviest rain in the city will also arrive tonight, which could slow drainage in low-lying areas.

PSEG Long Island said Saturday morning that it had restored power to more than 23,000 customers since 7 a.m. Friday, and that more than 850 line workers, tree trimmers and other field staff were responding, according to a storm update. The utility said the hardest-hit areas were the Town of Huntington and the South Shore of western Suffolk County.

PSEG Long Island warned that more outages are likely as the wind and rain continue, and that strong winds could temporarily slow repairs because crews can't safely work in bucket trucks in high gusts.

Floodwater swept through the streets of Surf City, N.J., on Saturday and got into some homes, the Associated Press reported. In Manasquan, about 34 miles up the coast, roads were also underwater, and Mayor Mike Mangan said he expected "a lot of water in the streets for a long time."

In Sea Bright, Mayor Brian Kelly said he expected this storm to be worse than the one or two floods the borough typically sees each year.

"I think this one will be closer to an Irene-scale flooding event," Kelly told the AP, referring to the 2011 hurricane. "I hope I'm wrong, but that's my gut feeling."

The borough opened its recreation center for residents who evacuate.

Nor'easters are common in the fall, but this one arrived while trees are still full of leaves, National Weather Service meteorologist Matthew Belk told the AP. Leaves catch more wind, which raises the risk of falling limbs, power outages and debris on roads.

The storm's north-northeast winds are also unusual, which state officials in New York said could make wind damage worse, according to Gov. Kathy Hochul's office.

The southern shores of Queens, Nassau County and southwestern Suffolk County could see up to 3.5 feet of floodwater in the most vulnerable spots, Gov. Kathy Hochul's office said Saturday. The Long Island Rail Road's Long Beach branch faces delays and partial suspensions because of flooded tracks, and several Queens bus routes are detouring around flooded streets.

NYC Emergency Management just wrapped a coordination call with the National Weather Service and City agencies. Here's where things stand and what's ahead.

What's happened so far⁰🌧️ About half an inch to an inch of rain has fallen across the city.⁰🌬️ Gusts have reached 45 mph…

— NYC Emergency Management (@nycemergencymgt) September 26, 2026

New York City's heaviest rain is expected to begin around 8 p.m. Saturday and continue into Sunday morning, NYC Emergency Management said after a coordination call with the National Weather Service. Bands of rain could fall at up to an inch an hour, with some neighborhoods getting 2 to 3 inches overnight and isolated flash flooding possible.

Officials called tonight through late Sunday morning the worst time to travel. Gusts of 45 to 55 mph are expected to continue, with an isolated gust near 60 mph possible, bringing more downed trees and outages.

The next high tide arrives around 8:15 to 9 p.m. on the city's south shore and near midnight along Long Island Sound, with moderate flooding expected in Jamaica Bay and the Rockaways. Sunday's midday tide could bring moderate flooding to the coastal Bronx and northern Queens, including parts of Flushing and Astoria, officials said.

Residents can report damage at reportdamage.nyc.gov, and basement apartment residents can gov/notify.

About 84,600 homes and businesses were without power across New Jersey, Connecticut, New York, Massachusetts and Rhode Island as of about 12:20 p.m. Saturday, according to PowerOutage.us.

New Jersey had the most outages, about 30,500, led by Ocean County with more than 8,500. Connecticut had about 24,600, with roughly 6% of customers out in both New London and Litchfield counties. In New York, about 21,700 customers were without power, including nearly 9,500 in Suffolk County on Long Island.

Wind gusts topped 60 mph in parts of Long Island, southeastern Massachusetts and Rhode Island overnight and Saturday morning, according to reports compiled by the National Weather Service's New York and Boston offices.

Nantucket's airport recorded a 64 mph gust, and Farmingdale Airport on Long Island and Martha's Vineyard Airport both recorded gusts of about 60 mph. Weather stations at Eatons Neck and Stony Brook on Long Island's North Shore measured gusts of 65 to 66 mph.

Closer to New York City, JFK Airport recorded a 56 mph gust Friday night, LaGuardia 46 mph and Newark 47 mph. Boston's Logan Airport recorded 51 mph Saturday morning.

title: 5 arrested near air base used by U.S. in Iran war on suspicion of terrorism
description:
— U.K. police said Sunday that five men arrested in the middle of the night near an air base used by the United States during its war against Iran are being held on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act that appeared to involve three trucks.
London’s Metropolitan Police, which takes the lead on potential terrorist activities, said police received a call at 12:45 a.m.
fullText:
LONDON (AP) — U.K. police said Sunday that five men arrested in the middle of the night near an air base used by the United States during its war against Iran are being held on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act that appeared to involve three trucks.

London's Metropolitan Police, which takes the lead on potential terrorist activities, said police received a call at 12:45 a.m. related to the three suspicious vehicles that appeared to be traveling toward RAF Fairford, a U.K.-owned base that is operated by the U.S. under an agreement dating back to the Cold War.

Fairford has been used by American bombers for strictly limited strikes against Iranian missile sites under an agreement with former British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, who voiced opposition to the war after it was launched by the U.S. and Israel on Feb. 28.

Iran has previously indicated that a base used to attack its territory is a legitimate target.

Authorities are investigating a link between the Fairford arrests and Iran as one possibility.

The five men were initially arrested on suspicion of committing offenses under the Explosives Act in the Whelford area, which backs onto RAF Fairford that hosts the headquarters of the U.S. Air Force's 501st Combat Support Wing and the 420th Air Base Squadron.

Aerial footage from Sky News appeared to show a bomb disposal robot roaming between three white trucks. The rear doors of two of the vans were open and large black items could be seen scattered around. The robot appeared to be working toward getting access to the third truck.

Police gave no details as to the nationality of those arrested. Suspects arrested under the Terrorism Act 2000 can be detained for up to 14 days without charge, compared to the 24-hour limit for standard arrests, without an extension application.

"We are in the early stages of an investigation, and five men remain in custody," said Vicki Evans, the Met's counterterrorism policing senior national coordinator.

Evans said a 400-meter (yard) cordon has been put in place around the three vehicles that raised suspicion while the army conducts examinations. As a precaution, around 85 households have been evacuated whilst these examinations take place. Some have been taken to a nearby recreation center.

U.S. President Donald Trump heaped praise on those involved with the arrests.

"It was an amazing job. We had them under investigation. They were looking to do big damage to our fort. And working with the British worked out great," he told reporters in Chicago. "We had them under view for a long time and we got them."

And British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he knew the incident would be "deeply concerning" for many. In a post on social media, Burnham thanked police and the armed forces for their response and said he was grateful to the residents who have been evacuated from their homes "while precautionary checks are carried out."

He urged people "not to speculate while the authorities establish the full facts."

The defense secretaries of the U.S. and the U.K., Pete Hegseth and Wes Streeting, have spoken about the incident.

Under the terms agreed, the U.K. government allowed the American military to use Fairford purely for defensive purposes, such as striking Iranian missile sites.

British security officials say proxies linked to Iran have been behind a string of arson and sabotage attempts in the U.K. and other countries, many of them targeting the Jewish community. They have previously warned that Tehran could expand its targets in the U.K. if conflicts in the Middle East continue.

The arrests come at a time of heightened tensions around the threat from hostile states to the U.K., with Russia and Iran among those that have used proxies to commit crimes on their behalf on British soil. In March, officials said the number of national security cases involving activity by hostile states including Iran increased 50% in the six months to December 2025.

The local Gloucestershire police force said the situation appeared to be "contained" and urged local residents to follow the advice as the investigation continues.

Julian Tudsbery, who has lived in Whelford for 30 years, said a resident had reported three "suspicious vans" in the village early Sunday.

"There were several police, three police cars in the drive, and they said you need to evacuate, there's been a major incident, said he couldn't elaborate," he said.

A spokesperson for the U.S. Air Force said U.S. and British personnel "remain vigilant" and will take appropriate actions to ensure safety of all those at the base.

"For operational security reasons we will not discuss specific force protection measures," the spokesperson said. "We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families."

title: Pope Leo urges Catholic Church to face failings before meeting French abuse survivors
description:
Pope Leo on Sunday urged the Catholic Church to admit its own failings and heal "deep wounds" inflicted within its ranks, hours before he was set to meet victims of child abuse by priests in France. 
   Leo, addressing crowds stretching out over ‌a large field near the famed Catholic shrine in Lourdes, said the Church must have the courage to face its past but did not directly ‌reference abuse scandals in France that sparked nationwide shock. 
   "In order to heal the deep wounds, infidelities and painful errors that have occurred within (the Church), we must humbly place ourselves under the Lord's purifying gaze," the ​first US pope told an estimated 150,000 people gathered in the field on a sunlit day. 
   Leo is on a whirlwind three-city, four-day visit to France, where he has again urged the world to reconsider the development of artificial intelligence. He drew around 800,000 people for an outdoor Mass on the Champs-Élysées in Paris on Saturday.
fullText:
LOURDES, France, Sept 27 (Reuters) - Pope Leo on Sunday urged the Catholic Church to admit its own failings and heal "deep wounds" inflicted within its ranks, hours before he was set to meet victims of child abuse by priests in France.

Leo, addressing crowds stretching out over ‌a large field near the famed Catholic shrine in Lourdes, said the Church must have the courage to face its past but did not directly ‌reference abuse scandals in France that sparked nationwide shock.

"In order to heal the deep wounds, infidelities and painful errors that have occurred within (the Church), we must humbly place ourselves under the Lord's purifying gaze," the ​first US pope told an estimated 150,000 people gathered in the field on a sunlit day.

Leo is on a whirlwind three-city, four-day visit to France, where he has again urged the world to reconsider the development of artificial intelligence. He drew around 800,000 people for an outdoor Mass on the Champs-Élysées in Paris on Saturday.

Local Church leaders are hoping he will help repair the Church's standing after a 2021 report found that some 330,000 French children had been abused by Catholic clergy and lay leaders over seven decades.

In an earlier, ‌closed-door meeting with French bishops on Sunday, Leo did directly ⁠refer to "the painful scourge of abuse committed against minors by members of the clergy," according to a Vatican-provided text.

The pope thanked the bishops for the "courageous measures" he said they had taken to confront the scandals and urged them to buttress their safeguarding efforts and "continue ⁠on the path undertaken, maintaining the greatest vigilance."

VICTIMS SCEPTICAL PAPAL MEETING WILL SPUR ACTION

Leo has previously apologised directly for abuse scandals that have damaged the Church's credibility across the world. On a trip to Spain in June, he told bishops there that they must listen to survivors and offer them reparations.

The pope is due to have a closed-door meeting with seven French victims ​of ​abuse by clergy later on Sunday. Some survivors said they were doubtful the encounter would result ​in quick changes by the Church.

"I am quite sceptical that the ‌pope will solve the issue, at least not immediately," Michèle Le Reun-Gaigné, co-president of an association for survivors in western France, told Reuters.

"Things are moving very slowly," she said. "It isn't going to happen overnight."

Bishop Pierre-Antoine Bozo, the spokesperson for the French bishops, said the pope's desire to have the meeting "shows that we cannot ignore this issue and that it must always remain among our concerns".

LOURDES CONNECTED TO VATICAN SCANDAL

The pope's itinerary in France includes six events in Lourdes, a town in the foothills of the Pyrenees mountains that attracts some 3 million pilgrims a year for visits to a shrine to the Virgin Mary and purported healing spring waters.

The site is also connected to a ‌scandal that has dogged the Vatican in recent years. The shrine's facade has a series of ​mosaics by Rev. Marko Rupnik, a prominent religious artist with Vatican ties, who has been accused of ​sexual abuse.

Rupnik, accused by more than 20 women, is not known to ​have commented publicly on the accusations. Five of his alleged victims wrote an open letter to the pope on Thursday, sharply criticising an ‌ongoing Vatican trial of the cleric.

The mosaics, stories tall, have been ​covered for the pope's visit with large, ​muted yellow tarps. Arriving for the Mass on Sunday, Leo was driven in his open-top popemobile near the facade of the shrine and the covered mosaics.

The pope, who on Friday sharply reiterated Catholic opposition to assisted dying initiatives two months after France created a legal right to die for those with incurable ​illnesses, again mentioned the Church's pro-life stance in Lourdes.

Meeting with ‌volunteers who help sick pilgrims hoping to find a miracle in the shrine's waters, Leo urged them to remember the "profound meaning" of healthcare work.

"That ​is to care for a suffering person, not to eliminate that person," said the pope. "Medicine must never become the servant of programmed death!"

title: FBI ousts 2 agents who investigated alleged harassing calls to Stephen Miller's wife
description:
Stephen Miller, White House deputy chief of staff, and his wife, Katie Miller, attend the White House Easter Egg Roll on Monday, April 21, 2025. - Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call/Sipa USA
Two veteran FBI agents overseeing counterterrorism operations in the nation’s capital have been removed from their jobs and reassigned over the handling of an investigation involving Katie Miller, the conservative podcaster and wife of senior White House adviser Stephen Miller, according to two people familiar with the move.
Michael Burgwald, the special agent in charge of counterterrorism matters at the FBI’s Washington Field Office, and his deputy, Courtland Rae, were ousted from their positions by bureau leadership after investigators determined that allegedly harassing phone calls Katie Miller received from unknown individuals did not warrant further investigation, the sources said.
The field office team that reviewed the reported harassing calls determined they did not meet the threshold required for an FBI investigation, and no nexus to terrorism was identified, the sources said. This decision did not sit well with bureau leadership, and the two senior field office agents were removed from their positions, according to the sources.
fullText:
Two veteran FBI agents overseeing counterterrorism operations in the nation’s capital have been removed from their jobs and reassigned over the handling of an investigation involving Katie Miller, the conservative podcaster and wife of senior White House adviser Stephen Miller, according to two people familiar with the move.

Michael Burgwald, the special agent in charge of counterterrorism matters at the FBI’s Washington Field Office, and his deputy, Courtland Rae, were ousted from their positions by bureau leadership after investigators determined that allegedly harassing phone calls Katie Miller received from unknown individuals did not warrant further investigation, the sources said.

The field office team that reviewed the reported harassing calls determined they did not meet the threshold required for an FBI investigation, and no nexus to terrorism was identified, the sources said. This decision did not sit well with bureau leadership, and the two senior field office agents were removed from their positions, according to the sources.

Since taking office last year, FBI director Kash Patel — a fierce loyalist of President Donald Trump — has fired, demoted, or forced into retirement countless career employees who handled past investigations into Trump and his allies. Many of those forced out have filed lawsuits seeking reinstatement.

In a statement on an official FBI “Rapid Response” social media account established to tout the agency and respond to critics, Darren Cox, the senior executive who oversees the bureau’s DC office, confirmed the ousting of Burgwald and Rae, but denied the order came from Patel.

“This was a personnel decision made at the Washington field office level alone based on our constant evaluation of mission needs,” Cox said. “Any suggestion otherwise is false.”

CNN is attempting to locate contact information for Burgwald and Rae. The decision to remove them from their positions has riled many rank and file FBI employees who have been critical of personnel moves they view as highly politicized, sources said.

Burgwald graduated from the United States Military Academy West Point and was the recipient of FBI investigative awards, while Rae similarly rose through the ranks of the organization after a lengthy career in national security, sources said.

The reassignment of the two senior officials was first reported by Bloomberg Law.

CNN has reached out to the White House for comment. In a statement to Bloomberg Law, White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said Stephen and Katie Miller had no interaction with Burgwald or Rae, adding, “Senior leadership at the FBI determined they were stifling investigations into very serious threats and made a unilateral decision to remove them.”

Still, there is a history of the Millers expressing their displeasure at the FBI’s handling of personal incidents they viewed as threatening in nature. According to people familiar with an incident last year, the couple grew irate with FBI officials over pushback by career agents to use bureau resources to investigate paper flyers critical of Stephen Miller that were posted in the family’s neighborhood. Like several senior Trump officials, the couple later moved into military housing.

CNN’s Aleena Fayaz contributed to this report.

title: Stewards surprised Lawson with their verdict on 'rookie mistake'
description: Liam Lawson finds it hard to understand how his incident with his teammate did not lead to a penalty, but it is certainly not something he will protest. During the first Safety Car restart, not only did Franco Colapinto cause an incident that knocked Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris out of contention, but Arvid Lindblad also hit Lawson heading into Turn 1.
fullText:
Liam Lawson finds it hard to understand how his incident with his teammate did not lead to a penalty, but it is certainly not something he will protest.

During the first Safety Car restart, not only did Franco Colapinto cause an incident that knocked Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris out of contention, but Arvid Lindblad also hit Lawson heading into Turn 1.

Lawson ended up crossing the finish line, but was unable to score any points because of damage to his car. Over the team radio, the New Zealander was furious. He said: "Man, I love getting taken out by my teammate. That's pretty sick."

Unlike Colapinto, the young British driver was not penalized, and he ended up scoring important points for his team after finishing seventh in their battle for fifth place in constructors' standings against Alpine.

Lawson said after the race: "I need to watch it, but, obviously, we're coming into Turn 1. I had massive, like, boost lag, and I didn't have any power. So Esteban [Ocon] was next to me. I tried to give him space, and then I just got hit from my left so hard that it put a hole in the floor, and then we couldn't really fight after that.

Lawson's car facing the wrong way after being hit by Lindblad in Baku - Photo: Race Pictures

"So I don't really know what happened. But, obviously, from where I'm sitting, there's not really space to go through the middle there. So it's not ideal. Yeah. I mean, obviously, on the positive, we scored points as a team. We got very, very lucky today.

"Arvid came to apologize. He said he locked up and that he had nowhere to go. So, yeah, I need to watch it, but it's not ideal."

The Racing Bulls driver was also surprised that Lindblad was not handed a penalty. "Obviously, I'm not going to go and protest my teammate, but it's just, I don't know, I don't understand it because I got hit so hard that it put a hole in my floor, and I was just turning for the corner giving the guy space. So from where I'm sitting, I don't understand, but, yes, it's let's say it's great for the team."

title: Kickoff time, TV network now set for Georgia football game vs. Vanderbilt
description: The kickoff time and TV for Georgia football's homecoming game on Oct. 3 against Vanderbilt was determined late Saturday night. Here are the details.
fullText:
Georgia football's game on Saturday Oct. 3 now has a kickoff time and TV network determined.

The No. 2 Bulldogs will play Vanderbilt at 12:45 p.m. in Sanford Stadium. The game will be shown on the SEC Network.

Saturday is Georgia's homecoming game. It already was set for an early afternoon start, but the time slot and network was announced until Saturday night after games were completed.

Georgia (4-0) drilled Oklahoma 41-13 in Athens. Vanderbilt (3-1) lost at Auburn 21-15.

The Commodores have beaten Austin Peay, Delaware and N.C. State. The 35-31 win over the Wolfpack came after Vanderbilt recovered a fumble in the end zone in the final seconds when N.C. State was trying to run out the clock and take a safety.

The Vanderbilt game will be Georgia's third early afternoon start and second 12:45 p.m. home game this season. Georiga's 70-20 win over Western Kentucky on Sept. 12 also started at that time.

This article originally appeared on Athens Banner-Herald: Kickoff time, TV network now set for Georgia football game vs. Vanderbilt

fullText:
The Jets lost in Week 2 to the Green Bay Packers, and with the defeat Jets fan confidence fell according to our latest SB Nation Reacts polls.

The Jets currently are sitting at .500 with a 1-1 record. Our poll has a similar 50-50 split. It is a large drop from last week's 82 percent confidence rating. One might expect that after a tough loss.

It has been a constant through all of the years doing these surveys that a great win typically leads to a large rise while a disappointing loss leads to a large fall.

One thing that unites Jets fans is that Aaron Glenn deserves extensive blame for the defeat.

Over three quarters of fans who voted say Glenn deserves a lot of blame for the Jets losing to Green Bay, while over 95 percent say he deserves at least some.

title: “In Great Spirits”: Dream HC Weighs In on Angel Reese After She Was Cleared to Play in the Playoff Opener
description: Getting hit in the face is not going to stop Angel Reese from playing in her first-ever playoff game. As the Atlanta Dream get ready to face the Washington Mystics in the first round of the playoffs, coach Karl Smesko has hinted that they might have Reese back in action for the first game, as the Dream management has taken her off the injury report.
fullText:
Getting hit in the face is not going to stop Angel Reese from playing in her first-ever playoff game. As the Atlanta Dream get ready to face the Washington Mystics in the first round of the playoffs, coach Karl Smesko has hinted that they might have Reese back in action for the first game, as the Dream management has taken her off the injury report.

"She seems to be in great spirits. She's had a couple of really good practices. I think she's excited about being in the playoffs this time of year," Smesko said on Saturday, just a day before the Dream face the Mystics. "We all know how great she's been; she's been great all year, down the stretch, she's been."

There was some speculation around Reese's status after her abrupt exit in the win against the New York Liberty on Wednesday night. With just around 5.6 seconds left in the second quarter of the game, Reese took an elbow to the face from Liberty's Sabrina Ionescu.

The play was immediately reviewed by the officials, and the foul was upgraded to a flagrant one. While Reese came back from the locker room to make two of her free throws, she exited again and did not feature for the rest of the game, although she did return to the bench with around 6:19 left in the third quarter.

Angel Reese's got the Dream playing their best basketball right now. 

"She was cleared, but we made a decision that it would be smart for her to sit out the second half," HC Karl Smesko said after the game.

Having Reese back is certainly good news for this Atlanta team. They have qualified as the fourth seed with a 30-14 record, and Angel Reese has been a towering figure in their frontcourt.

Reese has made herself indispensable in Atlanta's tactical gameplay, averaging a career-high 16.4 points per game, but it's her contributions in the paint and around the rim that have earned her several WNBA milestones this season. Contributing 12.1 rebounds while adding 2.8 assists and 1.8 steals per game, she extended her league record for most double-doubles in a season, with her 32nd double-double on Monday against the Liberty.

This also moved her level with Hall of Famer Yolanda Griffith for 12th on the WNBA's all-time double-doubles list.

Earlier in the month, Reese became the first player in WNBA history to surpass 500 rebounds in a single season. She currently has 521 rebounds this season, and Reese has hinted that she has no intention of taking her foot off the accelerator.

"Anything that goes up is mine," she said on August 24. "I want to be one of (the best) when I walk away from the game. So just being able to … be consistent every night is something I'm looking forward to doing."

Coupling Reese's dominance in the paint with some efficient shooting from Rhyne Howard, the Dream has all the pieces to make a deep playoff run. With four different players—Allisha Gray, Rhyne Howard, Angel Reese, and Jordin Canada—scoring in double digits throughout the season, Atlanta has shown that they are not dependent on any one player for its output.

However, ruling out the Washington Mystics, who have been the surprise package in the WNBA this year, would be a mistake.

Riding on a young core of stars such as Sonia Citron and Georgia Amoore, the Mystics have shown that they are capable of beating any team on their day, and against the Dream, the Mystics have shown that they can contain Reese and Co. when needed, having won two of their three matchups this season.

However, Atlanta's 109-77 thrashing on June 6 is a testament to the Dream's capability when firing on all cylinders. They caught the Mystics off guard in that game, and that outing serves as a cautionary reminder of the Mystics' shortcomings.

title: Argentine ace was ready to join Barcelona this summer but the club did not prioritise the transfer
description: Barcelona’s summer pursuit of Julian Alvarez has been well documented, as the club tried all summer to lure him away from Atletico Madrid.But as soon as Barcelona learnt Atleti are in no mood to sel...
fullText:
Barcelona's summer pursuit of Julian Alvarez has been well documented, as the club tried all summer to lure him away from Atletico Madrid.

But as soon as Barcelona learnt Atleti are in no mood to sell, the club began exploring other options, including Alvarez's national teammate Lautaro Martinez.

Deco himself has confirmed recently that Martinez was indeed an option for Barcelona but the move never quite materialised.

Lautaro Martinez wanted to join Barcelona in the summer. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)

A recent report from Diario SPORT has offered some fresh perspective on Barcelona's pursuit of Martinez this past summer.

The report points out that Lautaro was always ready to join the Catalan camp this summer, as a direct replacement for Robert Lewandowski.

But he was also loyal to Inter Milan and was only willing to leave if Barcelona were able to reach an amicable agreement with the Nerazzurri.

Inter Milan, though, denied any real approach from Barcelona as the club simply did not have anyone to sign as a replacement for the Argentine international. As a result, Lautaro ended up remaining at the club.

Martinez was never a priority for Barcelona. (Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images)

The report adds that part of the reason the Lautaro deal did not go through is that Barcelona were never really serious about signing the Argentine.

Although he was identified as a potential target, the Catalans had always considered Alvarez their number one priority and had harboured the hopes of signing the Atleti star until the last minute.

When Barcelona did realise the Alvarez move wasn't going to happen, the club reached an agreement with Arsenal for Gabriel Jesus as a fallback option.

The economic terms of the Gabriel deal was very favourable for Barcelona and the player's salary cut meant it did not take much of an effort to register him as part of the squad.

Lautaro Martinez, on the other hand, would have had problems getting registered due to his salary package.

title: Celtic’s Liam Scales reportedly voted to take stand against Israel
description: Celtic defender Liam Scales is at the centre of a modern footballing controversy today as Ireland prepare to face Israel. The 28-year-old started in Ireland’s midweek defeat to Kosovo but attention ...
fullText:
Celtic defender Liam Scales is at the centre of a modern footballing controversy today as Ireland prepare to face Israel. The 28-year-old started in Ireland's midweek defeat to Kosovo but attention soon turned to the meeting against Israel in Debrecen, Hungary.

Last night, Bolton goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu elected to leave the Irish camp after advising that he could not face Israel as he takes a stance against the horrors of Gaza and the West Bank. Prior to the goalkeeper leaving, the Irish players were locked in meetings deciding whether to take action before finally voting on whether to fulfil the fixture.

As reported by The42.ie, Scales was one of a few Irish teammates to vote in favour of action while offering support for Bazunu. Despite this, the vote went through for the game to go ahead and teams are expected to line up this evening.

Liam Scales of the Republic of Ireland and Promise David of Canada during the international friendly match at Saputo Stadium on June 5, 2026 in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. (Photo by Minas Panagiotakis/Getty Images)

It remains to be seen whether Scales is involved in the match. Judging by social media, any appearance would likely lead to a blowback on the 28-year-old. The players have found themselves in the middle of a storm and the events of yesterday clearly highlighted that their football association were clueless as to what action to take. The report states that players were discussing what steps they could take in order to show support for the Palestinian people.

The fallout from this game will be far-reaching and hopefully Scales is not caught up in it. The defender has clearly made his views felt if it is being reported that he was one that voted in favour of some action. Hopefully he is not involved and he does not have to field any criticism. Celtic supporters have been vocal on the 'StopTheGame' campaign as they urged the FAI to take a stand.

Scales has made 163 appearances for Celtic, scoring 9 goals and assisting on 12 occasions. The County Wicklow-born defender has been a solid figure for Celtic since arriving back from a loan at Aberdeen. Brendan Rodgers really took Scales' game on and he has become an accomplished first team option. For his faults, he always continues to work hard and show for the ball.

title: Angry US golf fans react as Donald Trump’s plan for Sunday at the Presidents Cup is revealed
description: President Donald Trump will be in attendance at Medinah for the Sunday singles matches at the Presidents Cup. Donald Trump is a huge golf fan and, as a result, he attends many high profile events.
fullText:
President Donald Trump will be in attendance at Medinah for the Sunday singles matches at the Presidents Cup.

Donald Trump is a huge golf fan and, as a result, he attends many high profile events.

The 47th U.S. President was in attendance at his golf complex in Doonbeg, Ireland, to watch the Irish Open two weeks ago.

Donald Trump may be a divisive figure, but his love for the game of golf cannot be debated.

Rory McIlroy and Brooks Koepka both enjoyed Trump attending the Irish Open earlier this month.

And now, he will be supporting his fellow countrymen at Medinah on Sunday during the Presidents Cup singles matches.

And it seems as though the President of the United States has a special plan up his sleeve.

According to Golfweek, Trump plans to deliver a 15-minute (yes, 15-minute!) speech at Medinah ahead of the Sunday singles matches.

Many US golf fans are not happy with Trump's plan one bit.

Numerous angry comments were posted on social media platform X in reaction to the US President's planned speech.

"The usual jumble of un associated words hoping they form a sentence. 'Mumble dogface banana patch. Thank you for your attention to this matter'," one fan joked.

While another US fan said: "Who listens to this complete clown anyway?"

And the comments continued to flood in, with fans saying: "Something stupid no doubt! I almost would like the Internationals to win today just so we don't have to see this embarrassment tomorrow," and, "That will be the kiss of death for the US team."

"Well just like the World Cup he'll find a way to ruin it for the US," another fan exclaimed.

"Great. We're officially cooked! Everything this clown self-inserts himself into dies," one fan said.

While another echoed a similar sentiment: "Thanks for the heads up. I'll make sure to flip the station during that vomit spill."

Many more fans shared their frustrations that Trump is making the event all about him.

Some of the comments included: "He is such an idiot. No other presidents have given a speech. This isn't about him," and, "How about you fix the country instead of promoting yourself. Nobody cares what you have to say."

One fan questioned why Trump is planning the 15-minute speech: "Why? Why does he always need to talk?"

While another suggested that the US President's plans will adversely affect the American team: "Well there goes any comeback hopes. This guy just can't help making everything worse."

It will be really interesting to see the reception that President Donald Trump receives from the fans at Medinah on Sunday and, indeed, from the US Presidents Cup players.

title: Phillies Organization Announces New Stadium Name After Record Attendance
description: The Philadelphia Phillies will see a major rebrand in a key part of the organization next season.
fullText:
As the Philadelphia Phillies continue to praise the home field advantage afforded by Citizens Bank Park in their ongoing quest to secure a home playoff series, fans got a major update on the naming rights for another one of the organization's stadiums.

The Lehigh Valley IronPigs, the Phillies' Triple-A affiliate that has helped develop key players like Rhys Hoskins and Cristopher Sanchez, recently announced the adoption of a new name for next season as the team's fans continue to set record attendance figures.

Cardinals' Breakout Hits Leader Sends Front Office Contract Message After Season End

Earlier this month, the IronPigs announced that their longtime home in Allentown, Pennsylvania, will embrace a new title sponsor starting with the 2027 season.

"The Lehigh Valley IronPigs announced at a Thursday press conference that their home ballpark will be renamed 'Jefferson Park' beginning in the 2027 season," according to the official press release. "The IronPigs have been the Triple-A affiliate of the Philadelphia Phillies since the team's 2008 launch and will continue to play its home games — at what was formerly called Coca-Cola Park — at Jefferson Park for decades to come."

The change comes as part of a new partnership with Jefferson, which is building on a relationship between the IronPigs and Lehigh Valley Health Network. The organizations said the partnership will extend beyond the ballpark through community initiatives involving IronPigs Charities and other partners, though it did not disclose the dollar figure involved in the rebrand.

Coca-Cola, meanwhile, will remain an IronPigs partner and continue as the club's exclusive beverage provider.

New Mets Skipper Addresses $75 Million All-Star Immediately After Taking Job

The timing of the announcement comes as the IronPigs continue to draw substantial crowds. Their success at the gate has helped make the ballpark an important part of the Lehigh Valley sports landscape, in addition to its role as the Phillies' top minor league affiliate.

"The IronPigs have led Minor League Baseball in attendance for four consecutive seasons and 10 times overall," Nick Falsone reported for LehighValleyLive. "The franchise reached 10 million fans faster than any other Minor League team in history."

Now, that highly attended ballpark will enter the 2027 season under a new identity. Jefferson Park is also expected to host 75 regular-season IronPigs games, more than 40 nights of Illumination and numerous other community events next season, keeping the venue active beyond its connection to the Phillies' minor league system.

And for a franchise with a fiercely loyal fanbase, notorious home crowd and perennial World Series aspirations, growth for the Triple-A affiliate should be welcomed.

title: Who wins the gold medal if Asian Games 2026 cricket final is washed out? Rules and scenarios explained
description: Who takes gold if the Asian Games 2026 cricket final is washed out? Check the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) rules and seeding criteria.
fullText:
Who wins the gold medal if Asian Games 2026 cricket final is washed out? Rules and scenarios explained originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Asian Games cricket rules award gold to the higher-seeded team if the final is washed out entirely.

Teams need to bat a minimum of five overs for an official result; anything less counts as no result.

The 2023 Hangzhou final between India and Afghanistan already set a real precedent for this exact rule.

The Asian Games 2026 cricket men's matches are already underway in Aichi-Nagoya.

The Indian team, led by Shreyas Iyer, has already reached the host city and have started training with the aim to defend their continental crown.

However, rain clouds hovering over a gold medal cricket final tend to bring up one nagging question for fans: who actually walks away with the medal if the weather refuses to cooperate.

Unlike standalone ICC tournaments such as the T20 World Cup, multi-sport events like the Asian Games run on packed schedules with shared venues, which means reserve days for cricket fixtures are more or less non-existent.

That tight window forces organisers to lean on a fairly rigid set of rules whenever bad weather threatens to disrupt a match, rather than simply pushing things to another day.

For a match to count as officially completed, both sides need to have batted at least five overs.

Should interruptions strike during the chase after that five-over mark's already been crossed, the result gets settled through the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method, with gold going to whichever side sits ahead of the par score at the point play stops.

Things get trickier if the weather refuses to let the match start at all, or if it halts the chase before the chasing side manages five overs. In that case, the fixture is declared a no result altogether.

Here's where seeding comes into play: under Asian Cricket Council and Olympic Council of Asia regulations, whichever team entered the tournament with the better ICC T20I ranking at the entry deadline gets handed the gold, with the other side settling for silver.

MORE: Who are India's opponents in Asian Games 2026 men's quarter-final?

At the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou, the men's gold medal final between India and Afghanistan was decided through seeding.

Afghanistan had posted 112 for 5 in 18.2 overs when heavy rain forced a halt, and it never let up enough for India to even begin their chase.

With India unable to face the required five overs, the match was called off entirely, and gold went to India as they were the higher-seeded side, leaving Afghanistan with silver.

MORE: 'Gill's India is better than Dhoni's 2015 side': Virat makes bold statement

Here's how things break down depending on exactly when the rain strikes:

No play possible, or abandoned before 5 overs of the chase

Rain halts the chase after at least 5 overs are bowled

Match ties, but rain prevents a Super Over

Bronze medal playoff washed out

Higher-seeded team takes bronze
