title: Jeremiah Smith and Julian Sayin give Ohio State permission to win differently
description: Maybe Ohio State doesn’t need a historically great defense or a dominant running game this season. Maybe it just needs 20 players to be pretty good, because J.J. and Julian are great enough to handle the rest.
fullText:
For the past two seasons, Ohio State's formula for winning football games has been pretty easy to understand: Have an elite defense, surround it with an offense full of NFL players, and wait for one side or the other to eventually overwhelm whoever is standing across the line of scrimmage. Four games into the 2026 season, however, I think it is becoming increasingly obvious that this team is going to have to win differently.

While very little is objectively bad, at this point in the season, nothing Ohio State is doing right now — offensively or defensively — is even in shouting distance of the level at which Julian Sayin and Jeremiah Smith are playing. And while that is obviously less than ideal, it is certainly not a death knell for the Buckeyes' College Football Playoff aspirations. It just means that the players, coaches, and fans are going to have to adjust their expectations for what winning football is going to have to look like this season.

It would be great if every other position group could somehow become as dominant as Smith and Sayin have been through four games, but I think any objective observer can tell you that that's unlikely to happen this season. Instead, the goal should be for everything else on the team to become reliably good enough to complement Julian and J.J.'s greatness, which is essentially how Ohio State beat Illinois 42-19 on Saturday.

The biggest adjustment that I have struggled to get used to thus far has been with the defense. In each of the past two seasons, the Buckeyes led the country in both scoring and total defense, allowing 12.9 points and 254.6 yards per game in 2024 and a frankly ridiculous 9.3 points and 219.1 yards last year.

At this same point in those seasons — immediately following Ohio State's first Big Ten game — the difference is even more pronounced. In 2024, the Buckeyes were allowing just 196.5 yards and 6.8 points per game. Last season, those numbers were 229.3 and 5.5. Through four games this year, they have ballooned to 274.3 yards and 12.3 points per game. Those numbers are still pretty impressive, don't get me wrong, but not historically so.

After losing an absurd amount of NFL talent over the past two offseasons, perhaps expecting anything else was unfair. I assumed there would be an inevitable reversion to the mean, but I was hoping that the veterans brought in the portal, the experienced players who stuck around Columbus and waited their turn, and the athleticism of the young Buckeyes would be enough to keep the defense amongst the country's best.

Of course, there is still plenty of time for improvement, particularly as young players get more comfortable with their responsibilities, but Saturday illustrated just how far the unit still has to go. Illinois piled up 462 yards, including 199 on the ground and 6.0 yards per carry. Aidan Laughery alone had 113 yards on just 11 attempts. No one with double-digit carries and without a 75-plus-yard run should ever average 10.3 yards per carry against a Buckeye defense.

The defensive line is still searching for the right combination of players, and the linebackers are contributing to the problems against the run. Riley Pettijohn and T.J. Alford have both had moments this season where you can see exactly why the coaching staff is so excited about them, but there were also some substantial assignment failures against Illinois: missing run fits, failing to properly set the edge, over-pursuing ball-carriers, etc.

The secondary has probably been the defense's most consistent unit, yet even there, busted coverages and penalties continue to pop up. So no, this probably isn't going to be a defense that suffocates opponents for 60 minutes every Saturday; it just has to become one that gets enough stops to give Smith and Sayin room to win the game.

The same principle applies offensively. The offensive line was perfectly serviceable against Illinois. Sayin wasn't sacked, and when the pocket did break down, he showed the mobility that we have been waiting to see consistently since his first start. I still think Sayin has room to improve as both a runner and a passer, but his connection with No. 4 has already reached a level of greatness that nothing else on this team even approaches.

On the ground against Illinois, Ohio State ran for 151 yards on 32 carries, which works out to 4.7 yards per carry; serviceable, I suppose, but hardly the type of production that should dictate the identity of the offense.

And I think that is something Ryan Day and Arthur Smith have to accept. Coaches love talking about establishing the run to set up the pass, but with this team, that equation needs to work in reverse. Ohio State needs to establish the pass to set up the run.

Bo Jackson or Ja'Kobi Jackson touched the ball on the first six plays against Illinois, seven of the first eight, and seven of nine on the opening drive. It worked against an overmatched Illini defense, but I am still far from convinced that the Buckeyes' offensive-line personnel and the skill sets of their running backs are enough to change the game against quality opponents.

But the thing is, I don't think they need to be; after all, Jeremiah Smith exists, and he wears scarlet and gray. Illinois inexplicably decided to cover Smith one-on-one far more often than I ever would have considered sane on Saturday, and Sayin punished them for it. Smith finished with career highs of 12 receptions, 217 yards, and four touchdowns, while Sayin threw for 367 yards and four scores without an interception.

J.J. was targeted on nearly half of Julian's 36 pass attempts Saturday. Any time Smith is single-covered, he should be Sayin's first option. Hell, he should probably be his second and third options too. Establish Smith early. Force the defense to abandon whatever machismo convinced it that one defender could handle him. Make safeties shade toward No. 4, make linebackers worry about throwing windows behind them, make defensive coordinators devote an unreasonable percentage of their game plan to one human being. Then let everybody else breathe.

That — combined with Sayin's newfound tough-guy running persona — was essentially the offensive formula I was talking about at halftime on Saturday: Make opponents prove that they can stop the best quarterback-wide receiver connection in college football before voluntarily moving away from it.

That half wasn't perfect for Ohio State, but it just about was for Jeremiah Smith and Julian Sayin. I know Illinois' D is not what it has been under Bert, but this is the type of offense that I want to see. 

A bit of tempo, throw to set up the run, feature 4, Sayin having guts! pic.twitter.com/kFpyEDDY0W

Ohio State doesn't need its running game to become dominant. It doesn't need its defense to replicate the historically great units of the past two seasons. While those things would certainly be nice, it doesn't need every position group to become elite overnight. The Buckeyes just need 20 players on the field to be pretty good, because if they can manage that, Jeremiah Smith and Julian Sayin are great enough to handle the rest.

title: Patriots veteran WR named as top fantasy waiver wire add for Week 3
description: Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins is a strong option to consider off the waiver wire for fantasy football managers in Week 3.
fullText:
New England Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins has emerged as a player to target off of the waiver wire in fantasy football for Week 3.

Hollins has been an integral part of the Patriots' offense this season and has a prominent role on the outside with A.J. Brown out due to injury. Brown's current stint on injured reserve gives Hollins a chance to put up more numbers in New England's passing attack in the team's upcoming matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Sharp Football Analysis' Raymond Summerlin named Hollins as being one of the best wide receivers to add in fantasy football this week.

"I am not yet giving up on Hollins as a contributor while A.J. Brown is sidelined," Summerlin said. "He still ran a route on 77.8% of the dropbacks in Week 2. The issue was the Patriots only dropped back 27 times and Drake Maye attempted just 22 passes. They should get more push this week against a Jaguars secondary that has been shaky."

Hollins caught two passes for 18 yards on two targets in the Patriots' Week 2 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers. Despite having a quiet performance, Hollins is still an encouraging player for fantasy managers in need of a player who will see ample playing time consistently.

The Week 2 output was a decline from his Week 1 showing against the Seattle Seahawks, where Hollins caught four passes on five targets for 51 yards. His receptions dropped by two and his receiving yardage fell by 33 yards, leaving him with a total of six catches for 69 yards and no touchdowns on the season.

Hollins enters Week 3 with Romeo Doubs and Hunter Henry having prominent roles in the Patriots' pecking order after both posted strong performances in Week 2. Nevertheless, Hollins has upside, with the liability to lead the team in receiving in any given game.

title: This £9.5m capture has been the very best of the summer’s Newcastle United signings
description: How would you rate the Newcastle United signings? Such a busy summer at St James’ Park. So many arrivals and departures.
fullText:
How would you rate the Newcastle United signings?

Such a busy summer at St James' Park.

So many arrivals and departures.

I want to concentrate on the incomings though.

The Newcastle United signings that arrived to take on this 2026/27 season.

Newcastle United signings in the summer 2026 transfer window

£24.6m Ewen Jaouen
£43m Bazoumana Toure
£23m Sean Steur
£35.5m Aladji Bamba
£25.7m Lukas Hornicek
£29.5m Amar Dedic
£52m Nico Gonzalez
£55m Matias Fernandez-Pardo
£3m Ousmane Diabaté

I think the club have brought in some very good players in the transfer window just gone.

However, I think by far the best of the summer's Newcastle United signings was this £9.5m capture.

I will happily hold my hands up and admit that I had never heard of the 38-year-old.

Just as I hadn't heard of most of the players United brought in across the summer.

Only seven matches into the season I think fair to say it is very difficult to come to any firm conclusions about any of the nine players Newcastle signed. Some have shown better form than others, some have played a lot more than others. It is still though only seven games and we have plenty of experience as fans, of finding out long-term that players don't always turn out as they appeared very early on. This can happen in both a negative and positive sense. Some new signings have the fear factor, living on their nerves, taking time to adjust to a new club and often new country. For others it is a real positive adrenaline rush that allows them to hit the ground running. Over time though the early nerves and adrenaline rushes wear off and we very often see very different players longer-term.

With managers though I think that it is very different.

As Newcastle United fans we have a lot more to judge a new manager on in a very short space of time. We don't just have team performances and results to go on, there is so much else as we see how they handle themselves in interviews, in pre and post-match press conferences and so on.

As fans we are also well aware of the situation a new manager has inherited, the challenges he faces.

It is now 53 days since Matthias Jaissle was announced and I couldn't have been more impressed with what I have witnessed.

The very first real indication that we had a potentially very special new manager, was when he was announced on 5 August 2026.

I went to the Al Ahli official website to see what they had to say on their manager's departure and there was nothing, nothing at all. Strange.

I looked all over their official social media and eventually found this one sentence that Al Ahli posted on X/Twitter: 'Al Ahli Club announces the end of the relationship with its First Team Head Coach Matthias Jaissle following his resignation, and the payment of the release clause within the contractual period.'

Isn't it wonderful. That is, wonderfully bitter. This is a manager who brought Al Ahli unimaginable success. Al Ahli had never ever won the Asian Champions League and Matthias Jaissle did it two years in a row! My reaction to all of this, as well as finding it very amusing, was that it made me then believe to a far greater degree that Newcastle United had got a very good replacement for Eddie Howe.

Al Ahli obviously so gutted and bitter at losing somebody who has given them so much, they had reacted in this beyond bitter and childish way. I think this also went a long way to explaining why it took so long for NUFC to officially announce Matthias Jaissle, the more reliable journalists had stated that the delay was down to 'paperwork issues at Al Ahli' that was holding things up. Even though Newcastle United had met the £9.5m release clause to trigger Jaissle's release, Al Ahli spitefully delayed it as long as possible for the new boss to start the huge challenge he had in front of him on Tyneside.

Matthias Jaissle, due to the delaying tactics of Al Ahli, only able to start work with NUFC 18 days before the Liverpool match.

I know we can often take with a pinch of salt what any new manager (or player) says when arriving at their new club, but with our new German boss, it did feel a little different and this was somebody who could potentially really get our club.

Matthias Jaissle explaining on 5 AUgust 2026 why he jad agreed to become Eddie Howe's replacement: "It is an incredible honour to become head coach of Newcastle United. This is one of the biggest clubs in European football, with a unique history, identity and supporter base, and I am excited to experience that passion and connection first-hand. When Newcastle United comes your way, you take notice. The ambition of the club, the vision for the future and the opportunity ahead made this an incredibly compelling place to be. I have followed the club's journey closely in recent years and the progress that has been made is clear for everyone to see."

Matthias Jaissle adding:"I am incredibly excited about the future. I fully and unreservedly believe in this project, the ambition and the direction the club is taking. There is a clear vision, strong leadership and an exceptional platform to build on. My teams are built on togetherness, hard work, intensity and a passion to improve every single day. I will bring full commitment, full energy and a determination to give everything I have to help this club achieve its ambitions."

Matthias Jaissle talking to official Newcastle United media about the players he has inherited: "I believe there is enormous potential within this squad and throughout the football club. I am excited to work with the players, staff and leadership team to help take the club forward. I cannot wait to get started and will attack this opportunity. I give my complete commitment and total energy to bringing further success to Newcastle United."

It felt to me very much like Eddie Howe, when he took over. Somebody who would put his heart and soul into the Newcastle United job. As opposed to say Steve Bruce who players later revealed had given them (and the then manager himself…) more days off training than they had ever previously experienced at any other clubs in their entire careers.

The Newcastle United hierarchy also revealed that this wasn't some spur of the moment appointment that they'd never previously heard of.

Those at the top of the club making public that they had contingency plans in place for possible replacements if/when Eddie Howe ever left, the same as is the case with key players who may leave NUFC.

Newcastle United Sporting Director Ross Wilson reacting to the arrival of Matthias Jaissle back in August 2026: "Matthias' leadership style and football philosophy are strongly aligned with our sporting vision. His teams play high-energy football and we could feel his passion during all of our discussions throughout the recruitment process."

The Newcastle United Sporting Director going on to add: "He has consistently demonstrated an ability to improve players, build cohesive teams and create elite performance environments in his coaching career. His successes at Salzburg and Al-Ahli underline his ability to deliver results while developing a clear football identity. We believe he is uniquely positioned to build on the strong foundations already in place and help take Newcastle United forward."

CEO David Hopkinson also commenting on 5 August 2026: "Matthias is one of the most exciting and highly regarded young coaches in football and I'm thrilled to welcome him to Newcastle United. We have conducted a thorough process, and he has emerged as the clear candidate for the role. He possesses all the qualities we were looking for."

The Newcastle United CEO adding: "His track record of success, leadership qualities and relentless drive to improve make him an exceptional fit for Newcastle United. We believe he is the right person to lead the club into the next phase of our journey."

When you think how easy it would have been for those in charge at Newcastle United to fall into that lazy trap of doing that usual Premier League thing, recruiting some out of work character who has already been sacked at a number of other Premier League clubs.

If Newcastle United had gone down that lazy route, then they would have been given a far easier ride by the media. If you employ a British manager who has been around the block numerous times and who has loads of mates in the media, those journalists and pundits then rush to back their friend/associate up.

I remember way back in the 1990s when Arsenal brought Arsene Wenger from Japan and the media found it hilarious. Who is this?

More recently you have seen clubs such as Brentford, Bournemouth and Brighton appointing managers that leave the media puzzled.

Indeed, back in November 2021 the media found it astonishing that the new ambitious Newcastle United owners decided that their old mate Steve Bruce should be replaced by Eddie Howe who had taken Bournemouth from the brink of falling into non-league all the way through to the Premier League, then taken a year out to increase his experience and skill set following his resignation as boss of the Cherries after their eventual relegation after a number of years in the top tier.

Eddie Howe did an unbelievable job at Newcastle United and I feel Matthias Jaissle has every chance of doing the same.

Just like was the case with Howe's era at NUFC, Jaissle knows that the odds are against him due to the financial rules that exist in the Premier League and with the UEFA SCR limits.

Listen to the latest episode of The Mag Pod! Join Jamie, Simon, and Hutch for their quality unfiltered Newcastle United debate.

title: Why 60 games is magic number in MLB's imminent lockout | Nightengale's Nobteook
description: MLB is heading for a lockout that could last months into the 2027 season.
fullText:
A growing number of executives believe that the 2027 Major League Baseball season will begin around Memorial Day weekend next year considering that if 60 or more games are cancelled next season, players will miss about four paychecks and national TV contracts would be extended through 2029.

The collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1, with the league demanding a hard salary cap and that idea being an absolute non-starter for the players.

The 2021-22 lockout was the longest in history at 99 days, but the two sides agreed on a deal that preserved a full 162-game season.

– While manager Dan Wilson will be blamed for the Seattle Mariners' embarrassing season and is expected to pay the price by being fired as early as Monday, Jerry Dipoto, the Mariners' president of baseball operations, is under heavy scrutiny.

Dipoto doesn't appear to be in jeopardy of being fired, but critics point out that the Mariners have reached the postseason just twice in his 11-year tenure, and veteran catcher Cal Raleigh went public about the Mariners' cultural woes .

"I think it was a collective failure, unfortunately,'' Raleigh told reporters. "It's going to take a lot of people having some self-reflection, myself included, on the direction of where we're heading, what we want to be, and who we want to be as a team. What is our team identity? I don't feel like there was one this year….''

The Mariners have plenty of disgruntled employees, with everyone from assistant GMs to equipment managers to strength and conditioning coaches being fired in recent years. And if the Mariners don't reach the postseason next year, those fingers will be pointed directly at Dipoto.

– Former Texas Rangers GM Jon Daniels, who guided the Rangers to back-to-back pennants, pulled himself out of consideration for the Athletics' GM vacancy for family reasons. Daniels, who has two kids in college and one in high school, was flattered by the opportunity, but enjoys his job as a senior advisor in baseball operations for the Tampa Bay Rays.

– The easy solution to avoid another Alex Bregman incident (suffering facial fractures when hit by a foul ball getting ready to hit), MLB executives say, is for the hitter in the on-deck circle to stand on the same side the batter is hitting. So, if Bregman had been standing on the other side of the field from left-handed hitting Michael Busch, the accident could have been prevented.

– The World Baseball Classic took a massive hit this week when 2025 Cy Young winner Paul Skenes blamed his participation in this year's WBC for his massive struggles, with San Francisco Giants ace Logan Webb also suffering his worst season.

Skenes threw 75 pitches at 95-mph or faster during the WBC, topping out at 99.7-mph. He didn't reach that velocity the entire season, with his fastball down 2-mph from his rookie season in 2024.

"It definitely affected the year," Skenes told reporters. "Unfortunately, I don't think I'm the only one."

The WBC is scheduled to resume in 2030, two years after the Olympics, but GMs are hoping that MLB could change the format to have at least the final rounds played during the All-Star break, to avoid the rash of pitching injuries when arms simply aren't ready in March.

– Dave Dombrowski, Phillies president of baseball operations, preaches the importance of veteran clubhouse leadership, believing it's essential for teams with postseason aspirations.

"I think veteran leadership is extremely important," Dombrowski tells USA TODAY Sports. "Not everybody necessarily agrees with this, but veteran leadership on what it takes to win."

Dombrowski has leaders Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper in Philadelphia, had Dustin Pedroia and Mookie Betts in Boston, Victor Martinez, Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander in Detroit, and insists they wouldn't have won the 1997 World Series without Darren Daulton and Craig Counsell in Florida.

– What a storybook ending to Justin Verlander's Hall of Fame career, not only showing flashes of his greatness in his final outing, but having his 7-year-old daughter wearing a Tigers jersey with her dad's name and number, running to the mound to hug him after being lifted from the game. Verlander stood on the mound sobbing.

"That hit me,'' Verlander said, "like a ton of bricks."

– San Diego Padres catcher Ethan Salas, 20 years, 116 days, who was not old enough to drink during the Padres' clinching celebration, so the Padres gave him a bucket containing apple cider, baby bottles and a tiny jersey with a letterboard that read: BABY'S FIRST CLINCHMAS.

Salas will be the youngest catcher in baseball history to participate in the postseason.

– Hall of Fame shortstop Barry Larkin raised some eyebrows when he criticized the Reds' front office in his final broadcast, which drew strong support from former Reds All-Star MVP Joey Votto

"I think these last three weeks of baseball playing against some of the better teams that are going to be going to the postseason really illustrate how far we are behind at this big-league level," Larkin said. "Change has to happen. This city deserves better than that, and I know every player down there feels that. But something has to give. We have to get better because we are so, so far behind.''

The ownership group announced that GM Nick Krall and his staff are returning for 2027.

– It's hard to believe that with more than 125 years of co-existence, this will be only the fourth postseason that the Cubs and White Sox have played in together, and they clinched their postseason berths just two minutes apart on Thursday.

– Miami Marlins Gold Glove infielder Javier Sanoja has had a surreal year. It began when he scored the winning run for Venezuela in their WBC championship game, and continued through the season, hitting  .294, including a league-leading .339 since Aug. 1. He's also the only National League position player to play in 10 or more games at five different positions this season (22 games at second, 117 at third, 10 at shortstop, 10 in left field and 14 in right field).

The highlight, though, Sanoja tells USA TODAY Sports, will always be winning the gold medal for his country.

"It meant so much for our country, and our people who are such big fans of the game," Sanoja said. "Every city I go, someone in the stands is congratulating me for the championship. It fills me with a lot of emotion. It's a night I'll never forget as long as I live."

– There's just something about September that brings out the best in the Guardians. They have won eight of their last nine games entering Saturday, and are 83-48 in September since the 2022 season_second-best in the AL behind only the Yankees.

– The Chicago White Sox, who grabbed Luis Castillo at the trade deadline, need to find a way to fix him in 2027 or else they just wasted $20 million. He was an albatross on their staff since his acquisition, going 1-2 with an 8.42 ERA in nine appearances.

– You can expect Red Sox rookie Payton Tolle to be a key to their hopes of defeating the Yankees in the wild-card round. Tolle now only has a 2.44 ERA in his last eight starts, but he has given up just one run and four hits in 13 innings with 18 strikeouts in his two starts against the Yankees this year.

– The Guardians are the first team to reach the postseason without a single qualifying player hitting .300 or hitting 20 homers or driving in 75 runs or stealing 40 bases, according to OptaSTATS.

– Randal Grichuk, who was released by the Yankees and signed a $1.25 million contract, has been an absolute godsend for the White Sox.

Grichuk signed with the White Sox on May 4 after Austin Hays suffered a left calf strain, and has hit .304 with 14 homers and 41 RBIs for the Sox, slashing .400/.408/.733 with four doubles, three home runs and nine RBIs in his last 15 games entering Saturday.

"He's obviously responded to the opportunity here, taking advantage of it," White Sox manager Will Venable told reporters. "He's been as good as anybody in this league offensively."

– Former Diamondbacks owner Jerry Colangelo, who led his franchise to its 2001 World Series title, was not part of the 25-year reunion celebration last week but plans to have his own dinner party for the team and staff in November.

– If the Pittsburgh Pirates want to be taken seriously, they do everything possible to bring back Brandon Lowe, who's a free agent this winter. Lowe has hit 33 home runs, the most by a Pirates' player since Josh Bell in 2019, with his 19 homers at PNC Park the most in the ballpark's history.

– The Yankees cringe watching Ezequiel Durán with the Texas Rangers. They traded him at the 2021 trade deadline for outfielder Joey Gallo.

– This is the Astros' worst season since 2014. ... and yet may win the AL West with a losing record.

– The Arizona Diamondbacks can't thank the St. Louis Cardinals enough for giving them Nolan Arenado this winter. The Diamondbacks not only had the Cardinals pay all but $11 million of the remaining $42 million that Arenado is owed, but Arenado has carried the D-backs' offense, hitting a team-leading 30 homers with 85 RBI and a .803 OPS, his best season since 2022. Arenado joins Hall of Famers Eddie Mathews and Mike Schmidt as the only third basemen in MLB history to have eight 30-homer seasons.

And the D-backs got Arenado for the mere cost of mid-level prospect Jack Martinez.

– How much does Aaron Judge mean to the Yankees? The Yankees hit just .227 and ranked 26th in runs per game without Judge in the lineup this season.

– The Rockies are the worst team in baseball once again. They became just the fifth MLB franchise to lose at least 100 games in four consecutive seasons, last done by the expansion New York Mets (1962-65). They looked pathetic in their final homestand getting trounced by the Diamondbacks.

They will go down in history as the first team to post the highest ERA in five consecutive seasons while also losing at least 100 games in four consecutive years.

– Congratulations to Pete Alonso, who became the first player in MLB history to hit 40 or more home runs in his first season with a team in the National League and the American League, and with 43 homers and 113 RBIs this season, could become the first player ever to lead both leagues in RBI.

– The Yankees are worth at least $12 billion after reaching a deal to sell 16% of the team for $2.6 billion to Apollo Sports Capital (ASC) last month.

– The San Francisco Giants' embarrassing season comes to a close by becoming the first team in four years to go an entire season without a four-game winning streak.

– In 2024 season, the Mariners' rotation produced an MLB-leading 92 quality starts. This year, just 66, with a 4.64 ERA the second half.

– Congratulations AL West, you just produced the worst division in history, with the division champion being the first not to have a winning record.

– Tropicana Field is a house of horrors to visiting teams with the Rays going 55-26 at home this season, and will have home-field advantage throughout the AL postseason.

– What's the difference between hosting a wild-card series and playing on the road?

The home team receives about $3 million in revenue from hosting the first round while the visiting team spends about $1 million with traveling costs.

– The Blue Jays' offensive ineptitude was alarming this year, scoring the fewest runs in MLB with only rookie Kazuma Okamoto hitting more than 15 home runs this season, and only two players with more than 10.

– Chris Sale produced the fifth-lowest ERA (2.16) at the age of 37 or older in MLB history, trailing only: Justin Verlander (1.75 in 2022), Roger Clemens (1.87 in 2005), Dazzy Vance (2.08 in 1928) and Spud Chandler (2.10 in 1946).

– The Mets not only lost plenty on the field this season, but also at the box office.

The Mets' attendance was down 14.8% from last season, averaging 33,901 fans a game, going from fifth in attendance to 12th, with their only sellout on opening day.

– The Yankees are expected to start Max Fried in Game 1 and Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler in Game 2 of the wild-card series against the Red Sox, which still allows Schlittler to pitch Games 2 and 5 in a potential ALDS.

– The San Diego Padres were 50-53 on July 23, with only the 11th-best record in the National League.

Now, they are in the postseason, going on a 15-3 run since Sept. 5, and will likely host the NL Wild Card series.

– Outfielder Austin Hays is in his fourth consecutive postseason with four different teams: Baltimore (2023), Philadelphia (2024), Cincinnati (2025), San Diego (2026).

– Diamondbacks starter Corbin Burnes, who signed a six-year, $210 million contract two years ago, will not opt out of the remaining four years and $140 million on his deal after ending his season on the injured list. He pitched just 10.1 innings in three starts this season recovering from Tommy John surgery, yielding a 7.84 ERA.

– Considering that first baseman Ty France may be the Padres' MVP this season, it wouldn't surprise a soul if the Padres' ownership gives him his $200,000 bonus for reaching 500 plate appearances, even if he's going to fall just shy of the incentive.

– The Padres may have had a losing record against the other NL postseason teams, but no one in baseball had a better record (59-28) against teams with losing records.

– Casey Mize's free-agent value has severely tumbled with his struggles since joining the Padres at the trade deadline, yielding a 7.46 ERA in 10 starts.

– If the Dodgers and Brewers match up again in the NLCS, they should have a bowling competition with Mookie Betts of the Dodgers and Brice Turang of the Brewers. Each are skilled bowlers who grew up with the game. Betts' parents each bowled and Turang learned the sport from his grandfather.

– Marlins ace Sandy Alcantara joined late Hall of Famer Phil Niekro (1978) as the only pitchers to lead MLB in innings pitched for a season and save at least one game in the same regular season since saves became an official statistic in 1969.

– Congratulations to Gary Matthews, Ralph Garr, Reggie Smith and Andre Thornton, who were inducted Saturday night into the Negro Leagues Hall of Fame.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Why 60 games is magic number in MLB's imminent lockout | Nightengale's Nobteook

title: Ladd McConkey Fantasy Week 3 Start or Sit: Lock Him In Against a Leaky Buffalo Secondary
description: An 0-2 Chargers team heads to Buffalo with McConkey 14th among wide receivers in PFN’s Week 3 rankings after a quiet week that looked like the ribs bothering him. He earned three targets on 22 routes last Sunday after seven on 18 in the opener, but no physical setback has been reported.
fullText:
An 0-2 Chargers team heads to Buffalo with McConkey 14th among wide receivers in PFN's Week 3 rankings after a quiet week that looked like the ribs bothering him. He earned three targets on 22 routes last Sunday after seven on 18 in the opener, but no physical setback has been reported. Buffalo has already let Nico Collins and Amon-Ra St. Brown clear 21 PPR points, and even a somewhat limited version of this receiver has a matchup there for the taking. He is locked in as a top-20 play with a nice floor and ceiling combination.

This offense looked like a machine for the first 30 minutes of the season, but one shot to the ribs of WR1 and nothing has looked even average since (0-2 record, outscored 52-28 in home games against the Cardinals and Raiders).

SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN's Free Fantasy Football Start/Sit Optimizer

To my untrained eye, he appeared a little bit hampered last week, something that earning three targets on 22 routes (seven on 18 in the opener) was proof positive of. I haven't heard of any physical setbacks, and as long as that continues to be true, I'm comfortable in locking him in as a top-20 receiver with a nice floor/ceiling combination in this strong matchup. Buffalo has allowed an opposing alpha receiver (Nico Collins and Amon-Ra St. Brown) to clear 21 PPR points through two weeks this season, and if McConkey is close to full strength, that's the type of game we can expect.

Even if he's somewhat limited, this is a matchup that is there for the taking, so patience isn't exactly the approach I expect to see from the Chargers this weekend.

title: Man Utd left sweating over key player’s condition as NT coach reveals ‘complicated issue’
description: Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus provided a concerning update on the condition of the Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes.The Premier League Player of the Year was naturally called up for the ext...
fullText:
Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus provided a concerning update on the condition of the Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes.

The Premier League Player of the Year was naturally called up for the extended international break. He was in the starting lineup as Cristiano Ronaldo's teammates went on to beat Wales on the opening matchday of the UEFA Nations League thanks to Joao Felix's solitary strike.

Fernandes was on the pitch almost for the duration of the game, only leaving his place to Joao Neves in the dying minutes.

(Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images)

On Sunday, Portugal will be eyeing their second win in the tournament when they clash heads with Norway.

However, Jesus reveals that Bruno might not be available for the contest in Oslo due to a 'concerning issue'.

"While in the game against Wales we came into it with practically all the players who were physically available, we came out of the Wales game with a complicated issue involving Bruno Fernandes. We'll see what happens by tomorrow," said the experienced manager ahead of Sunday's game.

"And from my experience as a coach, and physiologically, I'm also certain that on the third day not all players manage to recover."

Portugal manager Jorge Jesus revealed that Bruno Fernandes has been playing through pain and could miss the match against Norway:"While in the game against Wales we came into it with practically all the players who were physically available, we came out of the Wales game with a… pic.twitter.com/0riGmXmR6w

Interestingly, Jesus revealed this is a preexisting condition that the player has been carrying for weeks.

"Bruno comes with an injury from… from the night before. He already came with it. He's been playing with pain."

"I would rather not risk Bruno in this game and have him fully fit, with the physical conditions to play against Denmark."

Following Sunday's game against Norway, the Selecao will travel to Denmark for their third game of the international, which will take place on Thursday. They will end the window by hosting Erling Haaland and Co. next Sunday.

(Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Aside from his big performance against Ipswich Town, Fernandes hasn't been able to replicate last season's sensational form.

So the good news for United is that Jesus' admission may, fully or partially, explain why the skipper hasn't been at his best since the start of the new campaign.

But on the downside, MUFC will be worried about the playmaker's condition, and the fact that he's been constantly playing for club and country despite being hampered by a physical issue.

There have already been some question marks regarding Man Utd's management of injured players since last season. Benjamin Sesko has been the latest case, with some suggesting he was rushed back from injury while he hadn't fully recovered, and he now faces another spell on the sidelines

title: Tetairoa McMillan Fantasy Week 3 Start or Sit: Still Firmly Atop the Carolina Target Hierarchy
description: Carolina heads to Cleveland with McMillan 17th among wide receivers in PFN’s Week 3 rankings, and the 34-3 win over Atlanta is why. He took a 31.
fullText:
Carolina heads to Cleveland with McMillan 17th among wide receivers in PFN's Week 3 rankings, and the 34-3 win over Atlanta is why. He took a 31.3% target share and cleared 100 yards, opening with a 26-yard chunk on the first drive and then drawing an end-zone target on a quick slant that was tipped away. Jalen Coker earning another nine targets is worth tracking, and Bryce Young is having a ball throwing to two NBA-sized receivers on the perimeter. McMillan was drafted as a starter and should be viewed as one.

Jalen Coker is going to be a problem (another nine targets last week), but McMillan did showcase why most, myself included, are keeping him firmly atop the target hierarchy in Carolina.

title: Takuma Inoue vs Tenshin Nasukawa 2: Live blog and results
description: Takuma Inoue and Tenshin Nasukawa run it back in Tokyo!
fullText:
Takuma Inoue will once again defend the WBC bantamweight title against Tenshin Nasukawa in a rematch today from Tokyo.

Fight fans can stream the show live at 4:00 am ET on DAZN.

Inoue (22-2, 5 KO) beat Nasukawa (8-1, 3 KO) by decision 10 months ago in November 2025, and has since put in a pretty dominant performance against Kazuto Ioka. Nasukawa is coming off of his own pretty one-sided win, over Juan Francisco Estrada.

Has Nasukawa learned enough to turn the tide this time around? Will Inoue repeat and hold onto his belt again?

We'll be here with live results, fight-by-fight, in this post, and a live chat down in the comments section.

Official Scores: 115-113 and 116-112 for Malajika, and 115-113 for Tsuboi

Malajika wins previously vacant WBC super flyweight title

I don't agree with the result, I thought Tsuboi edged it, but I'm pulling up short of crying robbery, too. Tsuboi (3-1, 2 KO) started really well in the first half, but he absolutely faded in the second, possibly gassed out, possibly just that Malajika (18-2, 12 KO) is a good, experienced fighter with a style that can cause problems, possibly some worry over a cut he had. Probably, in reality, a bit of all of those things.

Obviously a setback for Tsuboi, but he has the talent to bounce back. It'll be about the mindset more than anything. And congratulations to Malajika; even if you don't think he won, as I don't, he didn't score the fight. He just went out and did his job to the best of his ability.

Official Scores: 115-113, 116-112, 118-110 for Matsumoto

Matsumoto wins the interim WBO minimumweight title, which will probably see him "promoted" to full champion sooner than later, as Oscar Collazo has that belt and still plans to move up in weight.

The first two scores were about right, I thought, and reflected the very good fight we'd just seen, where Acosta (17-1, 6 KO) definitely had his moments and fought his way into it in the middle rounds, but faded late, and overall Matsumoto (9-0, 4 KO) was the classier and more consistent operator. Tim Cheatham's 118-110 for Matsumoto definitely felt wide.

title: Colts' new uniforms: Indianapolis debut 'Anvil Strike' alternates vs. Texans
description: The Colts become the first team in 2026 to unveil their new "Rivalries" uniforms from Nike, Indy's featuring a blue helmet and anvil elements.
fullText:
The Indianapolis Colts are going to look quite different for their Week 3 game against the Houston Texans – and Indy fans certainly hope that's figuratively true on the field for their 0-2 squad. But from a literal standpoint, the Colts will be the first team in 2026 to debut their new alternate "Rivalries" uniforms from Nike with Indianapolis' specifically branded as "Anvil Strike."

To the uninitiated – or those who don't give a rip about football fashion – the Colts will be wearing an unfamiliar gray uniform and blue helmet. However, according to the team, and in keeping with the layered meanings so many new alternate kits seem to claim, "The Anvil is where history meets modern power. More than a gameday tradition, it stands as a symbol of strength, resilience and the relentless spirit that defines Colts football. Every strike creates something stronger. Every spark fuels something greater. From the field to the stands, that energy unites generations of players and fans under one enduring symbol: the Horseshoe."

The Colts have essentially transposed the look of their iconic helmets. The new ones are a glossy, metallic blue with the familiar horseshoe logo in white. Instead of a white stripe down the centerline – which, honestly, might look better – there's a black one instead. The jerseys and pants are technically "dark anthracite." The grommets of the horseshoe appear inside the striping down the pants and over the jersey's shoulders while "reflective accents capture the sparks and motion created by every strike" – whether to an anvil or from Jonathan Taylor's legs, presumably.

Think of them as the football version of the sports apparel company's NBA "City Edition" uniforms or Major League Baseball's "City Connect" jerseys. Nike has strived to create something that further strengthens NFL teams' bonds to their unique civic environments. And, as "rivalries" would suggest, all of them will be worn in intra-divisional matchups.

"Rivalries uniforms will celebrate storied local traditions and unite fan communities with designs unique to select cities and teams," Nike announced during the program's launch in 2025.

RANKING NFL'S 2026 'RIVALRIES' UNIFORMS Best to worst

"The designs are rooted extensively in the legacies and inspirations true to each team, serving as authentic, competitive expressions of community pride while giving athletes and fans an opportunity to connect like never before."

Eventually all of them will. This year, AFC South and NFC North squads will join the AFC East and NFC West teams that kicked off the program last year. Every team that has a "Rivalries" uni is scheduled to wear it once this season. The other four divisions will be added to the rotation in each of the next two seasons, and the "Rivalries" option then becomes part of a team's closet for the following three years.

title: Real Madrid, Barcelona on high alert as Haaland remains silent on Man City debacle – report
description: Manchester City have found themselves in serious trouble after being found guilty on almost all of the 115 charges relating to breaches of the Premier League’s financial regulations.The verdict has ...
fullText:
Manchester City have found themselves in serious trouble after being found guilty on almost all of the 115 charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.

The verdict has thrown the futures of several City stars into uncertainty, with Erling Haaland's situation attracting particular attention.

And clubs like Real Madrid and Barcelona are watching developments closely.

Can Real Madrid sign Haaland? (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

According to Diario SPORT, Haaland has chosen to isolate himself and avoid the media in the wake of the City saga.

The Norwegian cancelled his scheduled press conference with the national team, as he does not want to talk about City or his future.

Norway confirmed he would not speak during the international break, something highly unusual for a player who has never previously shied away from the media.

Both Haaland and the national team appear keen to shield the striker from a situation that could escalate into a genuine crisis with his club.

Notably, the forward had addressed the charges just weeks earlier, telling Time magazine he believed City's bosses and stressing that he was not personally involved.

Haaland has been quiet about Man City's debacle. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images)

The uncertainty surrounding City has inevitably sparked speculation over Haaland's future, and Real Madrid have long been admirers.

Haaland renewed his contract until 2034 in one of the biggest deals in Premier League history, and crucially, that contract contains no exit clause, even in the event of a sporting sanction such as relegation or a European ban.

However, the player's determination could change should City suffer significant sporting damage from any punishment.

The Norwegian has always made clear his desire to play in Spain at some point in his career, with both Real Madrid and Barcelona having shown interest in the past.

Any move, though, would be complicated. Without a release clause, City would demand an exorbitant fee, likely upwards of €100 million.

For Real Madrid, the reality is that their attack is already stacked, with Kylian Mbappe leading the line, Vinicius Jr recently renewed and Yan Diomande signed for a club-record fee.

Nonetheless, a talent like Haaland is one no elite club would ignore, and Los Blancos are monitoring the situation with keen interest.

title: Donadoni: Romano can’t save Italy at 20 — ‘What did we expect?’
description: Former Italy star and coach Roberto Donadoni defends Alessandro Romano: ‘If you think he can be the saviour of the nation, you are making the same mistakes as in the past.’Cagliari talent Romano m...
fullText:
Former Italy star and coach Roberto Donadoni defends Alessandro Romano: 'If you think he can be the saviour of the nation, you are making the same mistakes as in the past.'

Cagliari talent Romano made his senior Italy debut on Friday against Belgium, but one of his two misplaced passes led to Belgium's first-half opening goal.

Despite the criticism received after the game, Donadoni believes Roberto Mancini should continue relying on the 20-year-old midfielder.

"He's a very promising player, someone to invest in because he has a good head on his shoulders and undoubted qualities," Donadoni told Gazzetta.

Romano, a former Roma academy player, joined Cagliari on a permanent transfer this summer and scored on his Serie A debut against Parma in August, helping Cagliari win 1-0.

"In just a few months, he has gone from Serie B to the national team, a reality that's hard to compare," Donadoni said.

"Young players need to adjust to the change of level. What did we expect from a 20-year-old?

"Romano is serious, committed, and eager to train and keen to prove his worth," Donadoni, a former Italy coach, added.

"The starting point is excellent, and you have to build around a player like him, but if you think he can be the saviour of the nation or that young players can suddenly mature overnight, you are making the same mistakes as in the past.

"Elsewhere, they give talented players opportunities, but they are also patient with them. I'm not just talking about the coach, but about the entire environment surrounding the national team. Everyone, including clubs, fans, and public opinion, has to play their part. We need to give young players time to develop."

Mancini's Italy are now travelling to Turkey and will visit Vincenzo Montella's side in Bursa tomorrow, Monday, September 28.

Roberto Mancini speaks to the media at a press conference at Coverciano ahead of the 2026 September-October international break, which will see Italy take on Belgium, Turkiye, France and Turkiye again in the Nations League. (Picture: Lorenzo Bettoni).

"They are two well-prepared coaches, and the fact that they are both Italian shows that our coaching tradition matters," Donadoni said.

"Turkey did not do well at the World Cup, but they kept Montella because he showed that he has quality and because the federation has an important programme with him at its centre. That was the right decision."

Italy, on the other hand, have failed to qualify for the World Cup three times in a row, and many of those who lost to Bosnia and Herzegovina in March are still part of the Azzurri squad.

ZENICA, BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA – MARCH 31: Haris Tabakovic of Bosnia and Herzegovina scores his team's equalizing goal during the FIFA World Cup 2026 European Qualifiers KO play-offs match between Bosnia & Herzegovina and Italy at Stadion Bilino Polje on March 31, 2026 in Zenica, Bosnia and Herzegovina. (Photo by Getty Images/Getty Images)

"Mistakes and disappointments should make you stronger, not weaker. A professional must be able to handle difficult moments and respond to them," concluded Donadoni.

"The players selected to wear the national team shirt are good enough and deserve to be there. I expect those who were in Zenica that night to forget what happened and, instead, use that disappointment as motivation to secure qualification for the next World Cup.

title: Why Antonelli Adopted “Grandmother” Driving in Azerbaijan GP Unlike Fire Monza
description: Andrea Kimi Antonelli admits driving like a grandmother in salvage mode after not having 100% confidence in the F1 Azerbaijan GP. It was a rare off weekend for the F1 points leader, Mercedes’ Antonelli at the Azerbaijan GP. A mistake…
fullText:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli admits driving like a grandmother in salvage mode after not having 100% confidence in the F1 Azerbaijan GP.

It was a rare off weekend for the F1 points leader, Mercedes' Antonelli at the Azerbaijan GP. A mistake in qualifying set him back, and he never recovered from it, as he admits. The Italian accepted driving like his grandmother, in damage limitation mode.

It was a very different sort of drive, especially when compared to Monza. He revealed suffering damage after the re-start, which further pulled him back, but he still had enough to at least finish in the Top 5. "Yeah, no, I know it was bad positioning," started Antonelli with the media, after F1 Azerbaijan GP.

"But yeah, today I was driving a bit like my grandmother, just damage save mode, just didn't take a risk. Before making a move, I was making sure that I could go for it. At the same time, after the restart, I had a big floor damage, my whole left side was gone with the contact.

"So, after that, the car was very sketchy to drive and still tried to get to P4, but all in all, it's one of those days where you have to be happy with P5," summed up Antonelli, who explained why he was in the grandmother mode and not like his usual self that he showed in Monza.

It was simply down to confidence and pace in the car. He found no rhythm since practice sessions. It led to the mistake in qualifying and that set his confidence back by more. He was driving 80% of what he could do, and he realized early in the grand prix the difficulty level in a train of cars.

"Yes, definitely, because if I had the pace, it would have been different," explained Antonelli. "If I had the same pace as at Monza or in previous races, it would have been different. It would have been like just full attack. But today I realised very early that, first of all, it was a lot harder to overtake with a train of cars all in overtake mode.

"And then I didn't have the same pace as I had previously, so the mindset changed very quickly and also seeing so many people doing mistakes you kind of pulled back a little bit because today I just took advantage of everyone else's mistakes and just moved forward.

"Also, in FP1, I did three laps and then missed the whole of it, then missing half of FP2, FP3 I was getting into the rhythm and then in qualifying, the Q1 lap was actually okay. But then I did a mistake and then again you re-enter in the bad loop.

"Then in today's race, as I said, I didn't have the confidence and I just drove 80% the whole time. But also I think like being realistically, I wasn't there mentally to be able to push 100% as well because I just didn't have the confidence that I had the previous weekends, but it will be much better in Sepang," summed up Antonelli.

Azerbaijan Grand Prix, Thursday during the 2026 Formula 1 Azerbaijan Grand Prix, 15th round of the 2026 Formula One World Championship from September 24 to 26, 2026 on the Baku City Circuit, in Baku, Azerbaijan – Photo Eric Alonso / DPPI

With a win for Mercedes' teammate Russell, the gap is cut down to 66 now. It is still Antonelli with the upper hand, but the momentum can shift anytime. The Italian was relieved that he didn't suffer heavy damage, when he got caught up in the Alpine and Racing Bulls contact situation.

"Yeah, no, I saw the Alpine locking up, and I pulled back immediately," Antonelli recalled. "I was getting ready to do the switch back, but then obviously I didn't see Ollie coming so quickly on the inside and obviously I had to cut because I was still very close to the Alpine when I switched back.

"So obviously, I was lucky to come away with it. Not so lucky to come away with it with such a big damage, but all in all was still okay," summed up Antonelli.

title: ‘Most controversial…’ – Arch Manning interview over teammate draws bias complaint from Emmanuel Acho
description: Despite Colin Simmons having five sacks for the Texas Longhorns, Arch Manning being interviewed over him has caused quite the controversy. Simmons’ five sacks, along with his lewd celebration that earned one of the most controversial and talked-about penalties in quite some time, became a huge talking point.
fullText:
Despite Colin Simmons having five sacks for the Texas Longhorns, Arch Manning being interviewed over him has caused quite the controversy.

Simmons' five sacks, along with his lewd celebration that earned one of the most controversial and talked-about penalties in quite some time, became a huge talking point.

However, despite Simmons' noteworthy afternoon, Fox Sports opted to interview Longhorns QB Arch Manning instead, despite his unremarkable performance.

Emmanuel Acho took to X after seeing Fox Sports correspondents approach Texas Longhorns QB Arch Manning for an interview after their win over the Tennessee Volunteers.

Acho suggested that Manning was being interviewed despite an unremarkable performance and having very little insight to offer. He added that Colin Simmons deserved to be interviewed after being the team's standout performer.

"I can't wait for football coverage to evolve. We should be interviewing Colin Simmons post-game, the player who recorded 5 sacks & one of the most controversial penalties in recent history.

"Instead, we interview Arch, who basically says, I didn't play well & have nothing to say."

Arch Manning didn't do much against the Volunteers, with zero touchdowns while throwing for 201 yards and having one pass intercepted.

On the other hand, Simmons had an excellent game with eight total tackles, with six solo tackles and five sacks against the Volunteers.

The insinuation from Acho is that Manning, as one of the biggest names in college football, is being prioritised over players who outperformed him in the win.

Of course, many fans know that Arch is the son of Cooper Manning, the older brother of legendary NFL quarterbacks Peyton and Eli Manning.

Arch was also named after his grandfather and the patriarch of the Manning family, Archie Manning, another legendary quarterback who played for Ole Miss, the Houston Oilers, and the Minnesota Vikings.

As potentially the first third-generation quarterback in NFL history, Manning is a massive media figure and a huge name in college football.

And sometimes, that can lead broadcasters and media outlets to focus on him over the rest of his teammates, even when he hasn't played very well.

Hopefully, this media attention doesn't get to Manning, as it could cause ego and personality issues for him when he eventually reaches the NFL.

title: Why you should sit Chiefs WR Rashee Rice in fantasy football Week 3
description: Here's why Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice is a must-sit in your fantasy football lineup for Week 3
fullText:
The Kansas City Chiefs offense has been full steam ahead this season and will look to add to its impressive totals on Sunday against the Miami Dolphins.

Contrary to previous years, the run game has dominated the Chiefs' offensive strategy through the first two weeks. Tight end Travis Kelce has remained quarterback Patrick Mahomes' primary passing target, while several wide receivers have split targets and yardage.

Since his selection in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft, wide receiver Rashee Rice has been a favorite target for Mahomes. So far this season, however, the Philadelphia product has had a slow start.

The Dolphins' subpar defense could give Rice the perfect opportunity to break out and return to his dominant form.

The Chiefs' offense, which leads the league in total yards and yards per game, has relied heavily on running back Kenneth Walker and a rotating list of wide receivers. As a result, no single wideout has carried the load. Previously, Rice would have been a top target for quarterback Patrick Mahomes, but the former SMU Mustang has been having a quiet season so far.

With wide receivers Tyquan Thornton and Xavier Worthy slowly coming into their own this year, Rice will likely struggle to match last year's success. As someone desperately in need of a good wide receiver to start in Week 3, I will not be looking to the former second-round pick.

Mahomes has been spreading the ball around more than ever this season, and his growing trust in Thornton and Worthy has given Rice fewer opportunities. Rice may still be settling in after his eventful offseason, so a bounce-back game is hopefully coming soon.

Unfortunately, I don't think Sunday will be that game. I expect Rice to get about 40 yards on three receptions.

title: Texas vs Tennessee report card: Arch Manning, offense struggle; defense shines in SEC win
description: How the Texas Longhorns graded out in their 20-17 win over Tennessee. QB Arch Manning and the offense struggle, but Colin Simmons and defense gets high marks
fullText:
Considering the wild ending, Texas football won't soon forget its first trip to Rocky Top.

The No. 1 Longhorns (4-0, 1-0 SEC) opened conference play with a 20-17 win over No. 14 Tennessee (3-1, 0-1) at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn. But the victory came with plenty of anxiety considering the Volunteers scored a touchdown with 1 minute, 22 seconds left in the game and recovered the subsequent onside kick.

But Texas held on for the win and now gets a week break before its annual grudge match Oct 10 against Oklahoma in the Cotton Bowl in Dallas.

Here's how the Longhorns graded out in a 20-17 win over Tennessee.

Arch Manning was more efficient than explosive with 201 yards on 14-of-19 passing. But he didn't toss a touchdown for the first time in the past 10 games and he threw up a prayer to a double-covered Cam Coleman that resulted in an interception. He also absorbed six sacks while failing to get rid of the ball despite decent pass protection. His legs didn't lead to any big plays, but they did lead to two flags for an illegal forward pass.

Hollywood Smothers landed on the injury report all week and missed the game with an undisclosed injury. That meant Raleek Brown carried the load with 67 yards and two touchdowns on 17 carries. Freshman Derrek Cooper had the other seven carries by Texas running backs but tallied just seven yards.

Veteran Ryan Wingo emerged as Manning's most reliable target with six catches for 74 yards. Freshman Jermaine Bishop Jr., the slight but speedy five-star recruit, continues to make more and more of an impact; he had two catches for 34 yards. But where was Cam Coleman? The high-paid portal arrival had just one catch and missed some possessions with an unknown injury.

Sure, Manning holds the ball a long time in the pocket. But the Longhorns did allow a season-high six sacks against a talented Tennessee front. And the line didn't get much push against a questionable Tennessee run defense; the Longhorns averaged just 1.7 yards a carry and totaled 262 yards.

This would have been an A+, but edge rusher Colin Simmons gets docked for his tasteless sack celebration that resulted in a 15-yard penalty and kept a Tennessee drive alive. But Simmons had reasons to celebrate since he tied a school record with five sacks and Texas racked up a total of 10 sacks, which ranks second on the single-game school record list. Tackles Hero Kanu (four tackles, one sack) and Maraad Watson (five tackles, one sack) dominated inside, and end Lance Jackson may just be the most well-rounded defensive lineman on the roster.

Rasheem Biles, a Pittsburgh transfer, continues to make his claim on more All-American honors after a team-high 13 tackles and a late sack that helped seal the win. Justin Cryer (nine tackles) remains a superb sidekick, but the unit does lack depth. Both Biles and Cryer rarely left the field while helping hold Tennessee to 221 yards of offense.

Tennessee quarterback Faizon Brandon picked on Texas cornerback Bo Mascoe a little bit, drawing two pass interference calls and the late touchdown pass to Mike Matthews. Brandon completed 17 of 29 passes for 145 yards, and the Vols became the first team this season not to turn the ball over against Texas. Texas slot corner Graceson Littleton continues to impress.

Yes, kicker Gianni Spetic made both of his field goals. But those were the only bright spots for a unit that gave up a punt return for a touchdown for the first time in 13 years and failed to cover an onside kick late in the game that could have cost Texas the win. The Longhorns also had an odd illegal fair catch call on Ryan Niblett that wiped out a good return by Bishop.

Defensively, coordinator Will Muschamp produced a brilliant game plan that suffocated a potent Tennessee ground game, which had just 70 yards on 44 carries. Credit head coach and play-caller Steve Sarkisian for sticking with the ground game, but the Longhorns had too many penalties. Texas endured season-highs with 11 penalties for 115 yards, and that ultimately reflects on the coaching staff.

title: Chelsea quoted £86m to land top midfield target
description: Chelsea Transfer Thoughts as Manu Kone’s France Display Sends Value SoaringManu Kone’s profile has climbed sharply over the past week, and the wider market will have taken notice. According to Gaz...
fullText:
Manu Kone's profile has climbed sharply over the past week, and the wider market will have taken notice. According to Gazzetta Italia, the Roma midfielder has capped an outstanding run with another eye-catching performance for France, this time under Zinedine Zidane, and the consequences for any interested club, including Chelsea, could be significant.

The timing matters. Kone had already strengthened his standing with a decisive display against Inter, scoring twice and underlining how much his game has broadened in recent months. That attacking thrust has become a notable part of his identity at Roma, where he has been given greater licence to break forward and affect matches in the final third. It is one thing to influence games as an energetic midfielder, it is another to do so while adding goals and carrying a side through elite fixtures.

The latest development came in France's 1-0 win over Turkey, where Kone was moved deeper than usual. Rather than operating as a more advanced central midfielder, he was used in front of the defence, a role that asked different questions of his positioning, awareness and discipline.

Kone's output backed up the impression. He protected the back line, allowed others around him greater freedom, and delivered the balance expected from a holding midfielder. The defensive numbers were strong, the duel success rates were encouraging, and the overall performance suggested a player expanding his range rather than merely filling in.

For Chelsea, this report lands against the backdrop of previous interest. Roma are said to have rejected an offer worth close to £60 million last summer, while Atletico Madrid had also tested the waters at a lower figure. The implication now is clear, any future move would require far more.

Gazzetta Italia's line is that Kone is now valued at £100 million. That sounds substantial, but it also reflects the current market for high-end midfielders in their prime or approaching it. Recent deals elsewhere have pushed the ceiling upwards, especially for players who combine physicality, technical level and tactical adaptability.

Roma are in a strong position. Kone's importance has grown, his role has diversified, and external validation has arrived at senior international level. Clubs rarely welcome offers for players whose value is rising in real time, particularly when there is no obvious need to sell.

From Chelsea's perspective, the situation feels straightforward even if the negotiation would be anything but. Kone looks like a top-level midfielder whose stock is accelerating. Roma know it, France have now showcased it in another role, and the price reflects a market that rewards complete players at a premium.

As a Chelsea supporter, this is one of those reports that makes you sit up a bit. The first reaction is surprise at quite how quickly the price seems to have moved. £100 million for Kone would have felt ambitious not too long ago, but once you look at the way the market has behaved and the way his game is developing, it becomes easier to understand why Roma would hold that line.

What stands out most is the idea that he can do more than one job at a very high level. Chelsea have often looked like a side still searching for the perfect midfield blend, someone who can defend space, win duels, move the ball and still contribute going forward. If Kone is now showing he can anchor a midfield as well as surge into dangerous areas, that naturally makes him even more attractive.

There is still a shock factor around the number, though. Chelsea fans have seen plenty of expensive deals and that always brings pressure, scrutiny and expectation. You would want absolute certainty before going that high. But if the club truly admired him at around £60 million, then seeing him produce against Inter and then step into a different France role successfully only strengthens the case. Expensive, yes, but this feels like the profile of player big clubs fight over.

title: ‘Mum, where did my Robux go?’ The Roblox scam targeting children
description:
Criminals are trying to glean login details to harvest players’ in-game currency and personal data
Your 10-year-old son has started playing Roblox, when he realises all of his in-game currency, Robux, is gone.
When you try to find out what happened, he says he was recently promised extra Robux if he followed a link on YouTube. When he signed on at the site link, he was taken to the Roblox site as usual but there was no sign of the extra currency.
 Continue reading...
fullText:
Criminals are trying to glean login details to harvest players’ in-game currency and personal data

Your 10-year-old son has started playing Roblox, when he realises all of his in-game currency, Robux, is gone.

When you try to find out what happened, he says he was recently promised extra Robux if he followed a link on YouTube. When he signed on at the site link, he was taken to the Roblox site as usual but there was no sign of the extra currency.

He has fallen victim to a fraud where Roblox users – many of whom are children – are being targeted for their login details. With those details criminals can steal the virtual currency and players’ personal data.

Within Roblox, players use Robux to buy virtual items, such as skins or animations for their avatar. You can earn the currency within the game, but it can also be bought. At Roblox’s online store you can buy packages costing up to £199.99.

Using ready-made kits bought on the dark web, fraudsters create a fake login page that is identical in appearance to the legitimate Roblox site.

“The kid will enter their details and the fake website will actually redirect them to a legitimate Roblox page,” says Gerald Kasulis, the vice-president of global affairs at the cybersecurity company NordVPN. “So ultimately, the kid will get to where they want to go.”

Researchers from NordVPN say that over a seven-day period they found almost 200 addresses selling ready-made phishing pages that provided the tools to defraud Roblox users.

Often the links to the phishing sites are in comments on YouTube or TikTok videos or in chats on Discord, the chat app for gamers.

The message might say there are free Robux available if a player clicks on the link provided. Like many scams, there will often be an element of urgency attached, such as the offer apparently only being valid for a few hours, to encourage the victim to act without fully thinking through the consequences.

From that link, the child will be taken to a fake sign-in page that will probably be identical to a legitimate Roblox site in appearance. The address will usually contain the name Roblox, for example “Roblox-verify” or “login-Roblox”.

When they are on the scam site, the child will be asked for their username and password but may also be told to put in two-factor identification codes, says NordVPN. But then the child is taken to the legitimate Roblox site so they can play their games as normal, leaving little indication that anything is amiss.

Once they have the login details, the fraudster may sell them on or use them to transfer Robux to another account.

“One of the simplest habits is to encourage children to open Roblox directly through the official app or website rather than logging in through links they are sent,” says Marijus Briedis, chief technology officer at NordVPN.

“Two-factor authentication remains an important protection, but authentication codes and backup codes should be treated just like passwords and never handed over to somebody else.”

If your player has lost their Robux to a hacker, it seems unlikely that they will get it back. Roblox says that it is under “no obligation” to assist people whose accounts have been compromised, unless it is required to do so by law.

“Roblox does not guarantee that an individual’s account will be restored to its previous state, or that Roblox will be able to recover lost virtual items or virtual currency,” it says.

In “very limited circumstances”, Roblox says it may recover lost items or the value of them.

A spokesperson for Roblox says there are security measures in place to prevent phishing, such as two-factor authentication and a feature that stops criminals logging into your account from elsewhere.

“We continue to work on new ways to minimise the risk of account theft and actively encourage Roblox users to follow security best practices, including not clicking on links or downloading anything from unknown senders or websites,” the spokesperson adds.
