title: Shedding and raising pounds - Jones tackles longest run
description: Former Wales prop Adam Jones will face one of his greatest challenges when he tackles the Cardiff half-marathon.
fullText:
Former Wales prop Adam Jones achieved a lot in his glittering career as he became one of Welsh rugby's most recognisable cult heroes.

He is a three-time Grand Slam champion and a British and Irish Lions series winner, making 100 international appearances before retiring in 2018.

Jones will concede he was known for his scrummaging prowess rather than his running exploits.

Now aged 45, Jones will tackle one of the most significant physical tests of his life when he takes on the Cardiff half-marathon on Sunday, 4 October.

The Harlequins scrum coach has lost more than five stone (32kg) in his quest to "take himself out of his comfort zone".

Jones was inspired after seeing an image of himself when he was part of the Wales coaching staff in 2025, when he weighed in at 24st 7lb (156kg).

"When I was out in Japan with Wales last year, I remember the camera panning to me at the end of the tour and I was massive," said Jones.

"I thought I need to do something about this. I had a bit of gout, too."

Jones is typically dry and self-aware in his personal assessment.

"I've always been the type to look in the mirror and think I look like Arnold Schwarzenegger, when I'm actually far from that," he added.

"I'd go to the gym and do bits and bobs but my diet wasn't great and it was the old cliche of walking up the stairs being hard.

"I needed a challenge to change things."

Jones, who is running in aid of two charities, St David's Hospice Care and Prostate Cymru, has recently weighed in at 19st 7lb (124kg) which is close to his ideal playing numbers.

He admitted he had issues with his weight whilst playing, and recruited support from Wales chief Warren Gatland and fitness coach Craig White.

"When I was a player, I needed to be at a certain weight," said Jones,

"I told Gatland and Craig, 'give me a weight and I'll stick to it'. If I was at that weight, I could play well.

"I'd often crash diet as a player. If I had a bad weekend, I'd get back to my ideal weight before the next match.

"It was stupid. But I don't need to be crash-dieting for Six Nations matches or Lions tours now.

"I've got a slow plan. Drop it down slowly and training every day in one form or another."

Jones admits he needed to change his diet.

"Chocolate has always been my weakness," he said.

"I've got a sweet tooth. So I cut that out, as well as bread."

Jones started slowly as he adopted the "couch to 5k" approach.

"As soon as I started doing it, I saw the benefit of the process. It was fascinating to see and develop week-to-week," said Jones.

"I enjoyed that and started ticking off the little milestones. It is a brilliant process.

"The first run was a five-minute walk, then a 90-second run, and so on. You're not going straight in and doing it.

"Once you've got that 5k, it was a sense of achievement and you get that buzz after running."

He took to his new sporting endeavour so well he soon upgraded his ambition.

"After that, I was thinking of doing a 10k, but then I saw Cardiff was long enough in the distance that I could train for a half-marathon," he added.

‘Weirdly, I enjoyed the running part of training, so it appealed to me.”

Jones recently did a 17km training run, not something he did during his 16-year rugby career.

"It's definitely the longest I've run," said Jones, who with typical humour went on: "If you added up all the distances I've run in Test matches, it probably wouldn't be far off that anyway!"

Jones says Harlequins players and coaches have been supportive.

"The boys have been brilliant," he said.

"A few of them have sponsored me. Some haven't, but that's mostly the big earners.

"I think they're waiting to see me finish first and then the money might go up a fair bit."

The former prop also believes it is a positive for the players to see him making the effort.

"I'm putting myself in a place where it's uncomfortable.

"I'm asking them to stay in the fight and stay in shape when it gets painful, so it felt wrong if they couldn't see me do the same.

"I do have perspective. It'll be hard, but there's harder things to do.

"I always tell the boys here you're not working down a mine. My grandfather was a miner. What he did was hard.“

Jones has not targeted a specific time for the half-marathon.

"People keep asking what time I want to get, it's more about getting around for me," he explained.

"I reckon there'll be a few other 19-odd stoners knocking around the same time as me, so we'll have a little race.

"I'm competitive but I'm fully aware I'm not going to win and made peace with it."

He also has added motivation courtesy of one of the Harlequins players.

"Cadan Murley put into ChatGPT the other day to see what time I should run it in and said if I beat that time, he'll give me more money.

"I'm happy with the time it said because if I can do it under two hours and 30 minutes, he will double the amount."

Jones will be supported on the course by his wife Nicole and daughter Isla.

His father might also attend with Jones admitting he is "glad to see me get off the couch and doing a bit".

"I am a little nervous about it, but I'm buzzing," said Jones.

"I've had the race number from the organisation and it means things have got real. I looked at that and thought, 'What have I done?'

"I might go incognito in the race so no one can see how slow I'm going, maybe I'll put a balaclava or a daffodil hat on, so I don't get abused!

"But I've heard good things about the event and how people support you. I'm hoping the Welsh public will get me around the last few miles."

Jones also hopes he might continue his running career.

"I'd imagine I'll want to try another half-marathon somewhere else after it," said Jones.

"But let's see how this one goes first before I start thinking about running across the Sahara Desert and world marathons and all that."

title: Franklin wins three medals at European championships
description: Olympic medallist Mallory Franklin completes her return following the birth of her daughter with canoe gold and kayak cross silver at the Paddle Europe Slalom Championships in Ivrea.
fullText:
Olympic medallist Mallory Franklin completed her return to action by winning canoe gold and kayak cross silver at the Paddle Europe Slalom Championships in Ivrea.

The 32-year-old delivered a flawless, penalty-free run of 100.47 seconds to beat France's Doriane Delassus by 0.03 seconds and claim her third career European C1 title.

Victory marked Franklin's first individual medal since the birth of her daughter, having opened her week in Italy with a bronze medal in the team event.

"It's a really nice way to end the year. It's been a tough one coming back and getting back on the start line," said Franklin.

"I've been building throughout the year and it's just a nice way to finish it."

Franklin went on to complete a full set of medals on the final day, battling through the kayak cross knockout rounds under the floodlights to secure silver behind the Czech Republic's Tereza Kneblova.

Great Britain enjoyed double success in the kayak cross as two-time Olympic medallist Kimberley Woods took individual gold, winning the morning time trial in 48.02 seconds ahead of Poland's Klaudia Zwolinska.

And there was bronze in the men's K1 team event for Ben Haylett, Sam Leaver and Joe Clarke, to go with the one won by Woods, Franklin and Ellis Miller in the women's C1.

In the men's events, Clarke and Sam Leaver missed out on the podium in the kayak final, finishing fifth and sixth respectively behind Czech winner Jakub Krejci.

title: Why are Arsenal struggling to score in WSL?
description: Arsenal are already playing catch-up in the WSL title race because they are struggling to score goals. BBC Sport examines why.
fullText:
Arsenal go into their Women's Super League game at Stamford Bridge knowing defeat by rivals Chelsea would be a damaging result just four weeks into the season.

It feels like an extreme assessment but the Gunners know all too well that if they fall behind early on, it is hard to catch up in the WSL title race.

Renee Slegers' side are already seven points behind leaders Manchester City, albeit with a game in hand, and it would be foolish to give them further breathing space.

Successive draws against Crystal Palace and Manchester United have dented Arsenal's start to the campaign.

Their slow starts have proven to be their undoing in previous campaigns as their search for another WSL title has gone on for seven years.

In that time, they have lifted the Women's Champions League and Women's Champions Cup, proving they have a squad capable of winning major trophies.

But it is the same story so far in 2026-27 as Arsenal's shooting boots have been missing and their lack of ruthlessness in front of goal has proven costly.

They face serial winners Chelsea on Sunday (16:30 BST) knowing they need to get over the line this time.

"If I look at the last two games, not turning that dominance into goals and wins, is something we have to look at," said Slegers.

"We believe in the quality of the squad and their ideas. We can create in a variety of ways. When that starts clicking, it will be really good.

"It really is about the details in the final third."

Fox makes 'easy decision' to sign three-year Arsenal deal

Unanswered questions for English teams as Women's Champions League returns

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

Arsenal were tipped by many to win the WSL this season having invested in their squad in the transfer window.

Germany duo Lisa Baum and Selina Cerci boosted their attacking ranks, though England winger Beth Mead left to join Manchester City.

Slegers still has a wealth of options to choose from up front with Chloe Kelly, Olivia Smith, Alessia Russo, Stina Blackstenius and Caitlin Foord all available, as well as the anticipated return of Michelle Agyemang later in the season.

But despite an array of talent, Arsenal have struggled to score goals.

Across their first three WSL games they have had 56 shots and scored just twice.

They needed a 95th-minute equaliser to draw 1-1 with Manchester United and only beat HB Koge with a 93rd-minute penalty in the Champions League on Tuesday.

They had 70 touches in Crystal Palace's box and 79% possession but were held to a 0-0 draw by the newly promoted side two weeks ago.

"It's a combination of things. There's some details in decision-making and some details in the technical execution," said Slegers after their draw with United.

"It's also the ruthlessness in front of goal. I know the players want it. They want to execute for Arsenal.

"What kind of situations are we setting up? What spaces do we occupy in the box? What are the runs like, but also other moments in the game?

"Counter-attacking moments and set-pieces - those are also moments for us to be dangerous from so it's not only breaking down a low block."

Arsenal are creating chances so that is not the problem - but is there anything Slegers can do to change things?

The obvious question is why England's number nine, Russo, is not playing in that position.

Only Manchester City striker Khadija Shaw scored more goals in the WSL than Russo's 13 last season and she was second in European competition, behind Barcelona's Ewa Pajor.

But Slegers, who has often rotated Russo's position, has preferred her in the number 10 role at some point in all their WSL games so far this season.

It has not paid off for Russo, who is yet to get off the mark, despite attempting 11 shots, including 10 from inside the box.

In total, she has netted just three times in 507 minutes as an attacking midfielder, compared with the 21 she has scored in 2,913 minutes as a striker under Slegers.

Russo has created 1.42 chances per 90 minutes in the number 10 role, more than as a striker (1.27) but she has fewer shots and passes finishing in the final third, and fewer shots from inside the box.

Another striking statistic is that Russo and team-mate Blackstenius have never directly combined for a goal while the England forward has started in midfield.

Against Manchester United, as Arsenal trailed 1-0 and were pushing for an equaliser - which eventually came from full-back Smilla Holmberg - Russo continued to play in midfield.

When asked what Slegers' plan was, she said: "Basically, we were expecting to be spending a lot of time in their half.

"It was looking at how we could pose as much threat as possible in the box, hence why both Stina Blackstenius and Alessia Russo started.

"There was double threat in that position. We wanted to keep Alessia as high as possible on the pitch. We know she can do both roles really well for us.

"She's a fantastic number nine. Stina played her role. Selina Cerci also made her official debut. She has other threats, like her aerial play and instincts in the box.

"We have three [players who can play there] but the plan was to have two number nines in the box as much as possible for crosses."

title: Man City? I feel cheated - when do Stoke City get our FA Cup?
description: BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis explains what he and all Stoke fans are thinking after Manchester City are found guilty of the majority of the 115 charges they faced.
fullText:
That is what all Stoke City fans have been asking me since the news broke on Friday that Manchester City had been found guilty of breaking the majority of the 115 financial rules they have been accused of breaching.

While the process is far from over because Manchester City are expected to appeal, I have to say this verdict and the whole situation has left a very sour taste in my mouth.

Taking my Stoke side to the 2011 FA Cup final was one of the highlights - if not THE highlight - of my 50 years in football as a player and manager.

That day in May will also live long in the memory of all Stoke fans who followed their team to Wembley dreaming that they would win the greatest club cup competition in world football for the first time in their long history.

The club we were playing, Manchester City, were on their way to dominating English football.

At that time they had not won a major trophy for 35 years but they were a team that, in transfer fees and wages, cost well above anything Stoke City could ever aspire to.

Think back now, and I can still picture walking out before kick-off to see our end of the ground decked in red and white and hear the amazing rendition of Delilah from our supporters.

Many of those fans had come from all corners of the world, and had spent or borrowed fortunes to make it, just to say: "I was there."

For me, experiencing that game and occasion with Stoke City's owners, the Coates family, was really touching too.

Continuously, over many decades, they have helped to finance their own community's local professional team.

For Peter, Denise, John and all the family and friends who in good times and bad found the money and spirit to back the club, it was their one day in the sun.

It was the same for all of us connected with Stoke. This was our day, that day that many smaller clubs and their fans pray for.

Although we lost 1-0, our players were fantastic and gave, as always, a fully committed performance against the odds.

Yaya Toure, who scored the winning goal, was reportedly earning 10 times what we were paying any of our players and, on his own, had cost more than our entire starting 11 when they had signed him from Barcelona in 2010.

After the game, my disappointment was buried in the fact we had played a team full of superstars, and faced an elite coach in Roberto Mancini, and had just fallen short.

Today, I feel very differently, as I am sure people connected with the other clubs affected by City's successes in the same period, between 2009 and 2018, do too.

We lost, but to a team that have been found guilty of breaking the financial rules set out by the Premier League.

In doing so, they did not just beat Stoke in an FA Cup final, they collected a stack of titles and went on to completely dominate English football for more than a decade.

So, with those rules having been broken, what will the punishment be?

Well, I know all Stoke supporters will be demanding that City pass the trophy over and every club that has been affected by their actions will be considering their legal options.

I don't expect Manchester City to phone me or the club up and offer back the 2011 FA Cup and the winners' medals their players received.

I don't seriously believe any other trophies and titles will be handed back over either. A points deduction and a massive fine feels far more likely.

But I still feel cheated. Whatever happens next, we won't ever get that day back and the chance to celebrate around Stoke-on-Trent with the cup and medals we so honestly fought for. After breaking the rules, Manchester City got to do that instead.

Tony Pulis was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

title: Alcaraz wins after saving match points as Europe lead Laver Cup
description: Carlos Alcaraz narrowly avoids back-to-back singles defeats for the first time in 18 months as Team Europe lead Team World at the Laver Cup.
fullText:
Two-time Wimbledon champion Carlos Alcaraz narrowly avoided back-to-back singles defeats for the first time in 18 months as Team Europe took a 7-5 lead over Team World at the Laver Cup.

The world number three saved two match points before overcoming Taylor Fritz 6-3 4-6 13-11 in a dramatic deciding tie-break at London's O2 Arena.

It was Alcaraz's first singles outing since his late-night quarter-final exit to Ben Shelton at the US Open.

"The drop shot is part of my game," Alcaraz said after sealing victory with a trademark touch.

"In those really close and important moments, I tried to use it because it was a really good weapon for me in this match."

American Fritz, whose only previous victory against the Spaniard came during Team World's triumph in last year's competition, kept errors to a minimum.

However, Alcaraz struck 42 winners to Fritz's 20, bringing an audience that included Roger Federer and Andy Murray to their feet.

Facing match point at 8-9 down in the tie break, Alcaraz fired an ace before leaning on a drop shot to stave off a second. He converted his third match point when Fritz failed to retrieve another delicate drop shot over the net.

Earlier on Saturday, Andre Agassi's Team World had threatened to run away with things.

Alex de Minaur fought back from a set down to shock Alexander Zverev 2-6 7-6 (7-5) 11-9, while American debutant Learner Tien edged Italy's Flavio Cobolli 6-3 2-6 10-7.

Following Alcaraz's singles heroics, Zverev returned to the court alongside Casper Ruud to secure an important 6-4 7-6 (9-7) doubles victory over Alexander Bublik and Brandon Nakashima, keeping Europe ahead going into the final day.

Match wins are worth three points on Sunday, with the first team to reach 13 points lifting the trophy.

Europe are chasing their sixth Laver Cup title, while holders Team World are aiming for their third.

title: From turgid to thrusting - mixed start for new Scotland
description: BBC Sport Scotland's Tom English reviews a mixed start to life as Scotland head coach for Sebastien Pocognoli as his side open their Nations League campaign with a goalless draw in Slovenia.
fullText:
For 45 turgid minutes in Slovenia, some in the Tartan Army might have reimagined the Steve Clarke years as a time of plenty, the halcyon era of ambitious football when Scotland were an all-electric thrill-fest.

The opening half of the Sebastien Pocognoli regime was, as expected, disjointed.

It was also, rather unexpectedly, devoid of anything remotely related to what Pocognoli laid out as his non-negotiables - front-foot pressing, high intensity, speed of thought and mind, goal threat.

They had no shot on target and lost so many aerial duels that you stopped counting beyond the half-hour mark. They took 38 minutes to touch the ball in Slovenia's penalty area.

It wasn't like they were under major pressure - the hosts are a pretty toothless side - but neither were they accurate or energetic. Everybody who preached patience in the new era gulped hard. This was not good. We didn't expect champagne, but this was stale beer.

And then it changed, not so completely that Scotland roared and won the game, but they certainly cleared their throats as an attacking force.

Gilmour catalyst, impressive Welsh, but same issue for Scotland?

Scotland begin Pocognoli era with encouraging Slovenia draw

From being impotent, they became thrusting. That second half was as big a 0-0 rout as you're likely to see. Frustrating, but encouraging at the same time.

It will be agonising for Oli McBurnie that he's still without an international goal - he said he wouldn't sleep after failing to convert a one-on-one with Jan Oblak - but his second-half performance was full of good things; efforts on goal, link-up play, presence and danger.

Robbie Ure hit a post, Kieron Bowie had a terrific chance, but missed. The three strikers drew a blank, but as far as 0-0s go, it offered hope that more productive days may lay ahead with these guys.

There are two ways of looking at the draw. All 10 starting outfield players had a shot on goal, the first time that's happened since June 2022, against Armenia.

Scotland had 17 shots, their most attempts in a competitive game in more than 14 years. The flipside is that they have now failed to score in three tournament games in a row for the first time in almost 22 years.

After the break, Pocognoli dropped McBurnie a little deeper, in a pocket just behind Robbie Ure and then Bowie when he came on. He got Billy Gilmour to sit lower in midfield, where he had time to dictate, which he absolutely did. Gilmour tied it all together in the second half.

Pocognoli called it "two games in one game" and he was right. The subtle shift in McBurnie's and Gilmour's positioning brought Scotland alive.

It was an impressive watch; ambition, relentlessness, belief. No cherry on top but enough there to leave most folk happy about day one and motivated ahead of day two, against Switzerland on Tuesday night at Hampden.

McBurnie, not so much the prodigal son but now the forgiven one, had that big chance six minutes into the new half - the one he would have dreamed about. He created it for himself, winning possession and getting into a wonderful position right in front of an isolated Oblak.

He could have dinked it as the goalkeeper committed himself, he could have slid it home to Oblak's left or through his legs. Instead, he went for the flourish, trying to take it round the Slovenian and marking his return to the side after 2,005 days in the wilderness with a first goal on his 17th appearance.

Oblak won the duel. Painful, for sure, but a prelude to a stirring second half from the striker and his new-old team-mates. McBurnie played a slick one-two with the increasingly dominant Gilmour, who had his shot saved. Oblak was by a million miles Slovenia's best player.

McBurnie had a header fly over, Aaron Hickey had a header just wide, Bowie came on and had an immediate impact. He had three chances in eight minutes - a tame shot, a clipped attempt and then the big one - played in by Gilmour but pulled wide. In that moment, he joined McBurnie and Ure (after hitting a post late in the first half) in the torture chamber.

In the midst of all of that, McBurnie powered a header on goal, but Oblak was equal to it. That was Scotland's ninth consecutive crack without reply. They were utterly dominant but achingly goalless. So much encouraging stuff and yet just one point to show for it when it really should have been three.

Pocognoli said he was heartened by that second half. Scotland fans should be buoyed by the new head coach recognising the problems in his team and then fixing them.

With such a small track record to feed off, the subject of his tactical acumen was always going to be an interesting one - the ownership of the second 45 minutes showed that he's no slouch in identifying and changing the things that need to be changed.

Going with McBurnie and Ure up front was something of a surprise, but it sent a signal out that Scotland are here to go on the offensive rather than just defend their way to decent outcomes.

That didn't materialise in the first half, but it clicked in the second. It's a touch surreal that, at the end of another game when Scotland failed to score, there is a lot to be hopeful about in the men who are there to supply the goals.

McBurnie, Ure and Bowie are an exciting trio. When others are fit, there's Che Adams, Lawrence Shankland, Tommy Conway and Ross Stewart. Young James Wilson will have his moment at some point. New blood has joined the old guard and things should be better when everything settles down.

For Pocognoli, the next test is the biggest one. Switzerland, ranked 14th in the world, are missing some serious operators, but they are brilliantly coached by Murat Yakin and they're settled and formidable.

Their whole is greater than the sum of their parts. This will be a fascinating examination of Pocognoli's prowess. Win on Tuesday night and it's lift-off time.

title: White casts doubt on Fury-Joshua after 24 hours of chaos
description: There is fresh uncertainty around the proposed Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua fight - after Dana White said he did not know whether it would happen.
fullText:
Two days after the announcement British boxing had waited a decade for, Dana White - the UFC president and Zuffa Boxing chief named as one of the figures promoting Tyson Fury against Anthony Joshua - was asked whether the fight would actually happen.

White was speaking at London's Copper Box on Saturday, where British heavyweight Johnny Fisher beat Michael Pirotton on his Zuffa Boxing debut. But for much of the media in attendance another heavyweight fight dominated the evening.

Asked whether Wednesday's scheduled Fury-Joshua news conference in London would take place, White added: "I have no idea."

On Thursday, Fury and Joshua were officially announced to meet at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December, live globally on Netflix. By Friday, that certainty had unravelled.

A dispute over who is entitled to promote the event led to claims of contractual breaches, talk of possible replacement fights and another flurry of cryptic social-media posts.

Even by boxing's recent standards, the past 24 hours have been extraordinary - and not a particularly flattering look for the sport.

Netflix and Saudi powerbroker Turki Alalshikh's fight announcement was striking for who it included - and who it did not. The event was presented as a collaboration involving Alalshikh's The Ring and White.

There was no mention of Matchroom's Eddie Hearn, who has promoted Joshua throughout his professional career, or Queensberry's Frank Warren, Fury's long-time promoter.

White's involvement was not entirely unexpected.

The Zuffa Boxing promoter has been saying for weeks he would be involved in Fury-Joshua.

Hearn has been equally adamant he would not. After Thursday's announcement, Hearn said Joshua's contract specifically prevented White and American sports entertainment company TKO from having a promotional role, claiming Netflix had not been made aware of that provision.

Hearn said there had been breaches of the agreement which needed to be resolved and cast doubt on whether Wednesday's news conference would go ahead.

Fury says a similar restriction originally appeared in his own contract but was removed because he wanted White involved.

Warren has taken a more pragmatic position. Speaking to BBC Sport before the latest dispute escalated, he said his understanding was White had helped secure the Netflix deal and compromises had been necessary to get the fight made.

On Saturday, White was generally non-committal on the future of the contest but much clearer in his criticism of Hearn. "The guy who is supposed to be helping the fight has been hurting the fight," White said. "He hasn't done the fight any favours."

The uncertainty intensified on Friday evening.

Reports emerged that Fury-Joshua could be in jeopardy and alternative fights for 11 December were being discussed, including Ryan Garcia against the recently retired three-weight undisputed champion Terence Crawford.

Crawford appeared as surprised as anyone, publicly questioning the suggestion he could be fighting Garcia.

In a video posted on social media, he claimed Joshua and Hearn were "trying to pull out" and blamed the dispute largely on Hearn's objection to White.

There has been no announcement from Joshua saying he intends to withdraw.

On Instagram, Alalshikh posted pictures of himself with White and later shared a cryptic message in Arabic about somebody attempting to "stab you where you told them it hurts", although he made no explicit reference to Fury-Joshua.

Hearn, meanwhile, posted a picture with a shushing emoji and the message: "Bet against me."

For a fight negotiated so publicly for so many years, the familiar mix of claims, counter-claims and cryptic posts had returned almost immediately.

Among the media in east London on Saturday, much of the conversation centred around Fury-Joshua.

Who had heard what? Was the fight genuinely in danger? Would Wednesday's news conference happen? And, with White in the building, would he provide any clarity afterwards?

Instead, his post-fight comments only underlined the uncertainty.

White has been openly critical of Hearn, while the precise nature of his own role in Fury-Joshua remains at the heart of the dispute. That distinction could prove significant when lawyers examine exactly what Joshua's contract permits.

During Saturday's US broadcast of the Zuffa Boxing card, it was suggested White was helping Alalshikh on a personal level rather than acting as a promoter. White rejected that interpretation. "I don't know where that came from," he said. "That was weird."

And White offered another tease when asked whether he would attend Wednesday's news conference if it does go ahead. "I guess I'll leave that as a surprise," he said.

As of Saturday night, Netflix continued to list Fury against Joshua at the Principality Stadium on 11 December and said the fighters would attend Wednesday's news conference.

But the contractual disagreement remains unresolved.

The unusual position is that, little more than 48 hours after the fight was officially announced, one of the central figures in its promotion cannot say whether it will happen - or whether its first major launch event will go ahead.

There is too much money, time and work invested in Fury-Joshua for anyone involved to walk away lightly.

But if the past decade has taught boxing anything, an agreement does not necessarily mean the fight is safe. Fury-Joshua is once again waiting for another hurdle to be cleared.

fullText:
Iran stood firm Sunday on its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, despite US President Donald Trump's rejection of the proposal that had created some optimism for breaking the Mideast war stalemate.

The waterway is key to the world's energy supply and is now central to the conflict between Washington and Tehran, which was triggered nearly seven months ago with deadly strikes on Iran.

Iran's plan called for a cessation of all hostilities in the Middle East, including in Lebanon, according to Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, and fulfilling conditions in the ceasefire deal that fell apart months ago.

That agreement, which dissolved during fighting over Hormuz, called for the release of frozen Iranian assets, the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil and an end to the US naval blockade.

"Our conditions are clear, and any move toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent upon these conditions being fulfilled. We will not back down from them," Araghchi said on Sunday, state broadcaster IRIB reported.

"We have never closed the door to diplomacy or negotiations, but at the same time, we have never backed down from our rights."

But Trump said on Saturday that he rejected the truce deal.

"They want to make a deal where they open the Strait immediately because they're losing so badly," he told reporters. "They want to make a deal and I think that's fine. I like making a deal too."

Araghchi said on Sunday that the Iranians "saw the first reaction from the US president, but so far, nothing has been conveyed to us by the mediators".

"We are waiting for the mediators to convey the definitive positions to us, and we will make a decision based on them," the foreign minister added.

Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding in June that aimed to end the war, to reopen the strait and to launch talks on Iran's nuclear programme.

But the deal broke down shortly afterwards when Iran fired on commercial ships in Hormuz that it accused of deviating from its approved route through the waterway.

Iran requires ships to obtain authorisation before passage, citing security and sovereignty reasons.

Ships that refuse to comply are regularly targeted, while the United States sporadically bombs Iranian coastal areas in retaliation.

At the UN, Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan complained that the "international community has been absent" and is failing to live up to the responsibility to keep the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab open.

"The kingdom rejects any party's use of these vital passages as a tool for pressure, threat, or harm to the interests of states," he said, stressing the waterways' importance to global energy security.

His Russian counterpart, Sergei Lavrov, told member states that "Russia, together with other responsible states, stands ready to constructively contribute to stabilising this strategically important region."

In New York, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, according to his office, and said: "Iran has not walked away from the negotiating table but, given past experiences, it no longer trusts the United States."

Araghchi said at the UN: "Iran has conveyed to the United States, through Qatar, a concrete seven-day plan. If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, and normal maritime passage restored within seven days."

"The choice now rests with the United States. Iran does not accept coercion, threats or intimidation, and Iran will not surrender its sovereign rights under pressure," he added.

Hossein Mohebi, a spokesman for Iran's Revolutionary Guards, was quoted by Tasnim news agency as saying: "We will not cease punishing the US until Iran's seven conditions are met."

Mohebi had told AFP in an exclusive interview on Tuesday that ending hostilities in Yemen was also among Tehran's demands.

title: U.K. police make several arrests under Explosives Act in 'major incident' near U.S. air base
description:
British police announced on Sunday morning that several people were arrested "on suspicion of offenses under the explosives act" close to a major air base hosting U.S. forces in the southwest of England.
"A number of properties are currently being evacuated in the Whelford area following the declaration of a major incident," Gloucestershire Police said in a statement. "It follows the arrest of several men on suspicion of offenses under the explosives act.
fullText:
The village of Whelford is located around 2 miles from RAF Fairford.

LONDON -- British police announced on Sunday morning that several people were arrested "on suspicion of offenses under the explosives act" close to a major air base hosting U.S. forces in the southwest of England.

"A number of properties are currently being evacuated in the Whelford area following the declaration of a major incident," Gloucestershire Police said in a statement. "It follows the arrest of several men on suspicion of offenses under the explosives act."

The village of Whelford is located around 2 miles from RAF Fairford, which hosts the U.S. Air Force and has since February been serving as a key hub for American operations against Iran -- including for heavy bombers like the B-1 Lancer and B-52 Stratofortress.

"The Army's specialist explosive ordnance disposal team are currently examining a number of vehicles," the police statement said.

Local residents were evacuated to a nearby recreation center, with a cordon put in place. "We believe this incident is contained," police said. "We are working closely with our partners and are enacting the well-rehearsed plans we have in place."

A British government spokesperson told ABC News that Prime Minister Andy Burnham "is being kept updated on the incident in Gloucestershire."

"We are grateful to the emergency services, who have acted quickly to detain several suspects and put measures in place to keep the community safe," they added. "It would be inappropriate to comment further whilst investigations are ongoing."

British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting said in a post to X, "We can be reassured that this is being dealt with, and it is exactly why our emergency response teams and Armed Forces are on standby 24/7."

ABC News' Rashid Haddou-Riffi, Guy Davies and Lama Hasan contributed to this report.

title: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 27 dead
description: Gunmen torched vehicles as they fled the scene of a mass shooting at bar near Johannesburg  [Getty...
fullText:
Twenty-seven people have been killed in two mass shootings hours apart in South Africa, the latest gun violence to hit the country.

Seventeen people were killed when eight gunmen stormed a bar close to Johannesburg on Saturday evening, with 15 more injured.

In a separate shooting in the early hours of Sunday morning, 10 people were killed outside an entertainment venue in a township near Cape Town and a further 11 were injured.

South Africa has one of the highest murder rates in the world and has struggled to contain gang-related gun violence in recent years. Police have not indicated a motive for either of the latest attacks.

In Johannesburg, gunmen opened fire on customers outside the bar before continuing the attack inside and torching two vehicles before fleeing.

Police said thirteen men and four women were killed.

Deputy provincial police commissioner Maj Gen Fred Kekana said the attack may have been a retaliation for an incident last month, in which one person was killed and another wounded, according to AFP news agency.

Speaking at the scene, he said police had clear pictures and in some cases names for the suspects.

In Cape Town, five victims died at the scene and a further five people died in hospital.

No arrests had been made in either case on Sunday morning.

The two mass shootings came days after 11 people were killed in the city of Durban when gunmen stormed a house in the KwaMakhutha township.

Illegal weapons are prevalent in South Africa and gun violence has been a persistent problem for decades, with about 60 murders recorded every day in the country of 62 million.

But a recent spate of mass shootings has raised fears that the problem is deepening, with violence often linked to turf wars between gangs engaged in drug trafficking and illegal mining.

In February, President Cyril Ramaphosa called organised crime "the most immediate threat to our democracy, our society and our economic development".

Earlier this year the military was deployed alongside police in areas with the highest murder rates in an effort to reduce armed violence.

On Saturday a tenth woman's body was found in Ekurhuleni, to the east of Johannesburg, with local police saying they were unable to rule out a serial killer operating in the area with similarities between the deaths.

title: Cardiff seal opening Welsh derby win over Scarlets
description: Cardiff triumph in the first United Rugby Championship (URC) Welsh derby of the season by beating Scarlets in Llanelli.
fullText:
Tries: Roberts, Murray Cons: Anscombe Pens: Hawkins

Tries: D Thomas, Basham, E Lloyd Cons: Sheedy 2, Evans

Cardiff triumphed in the first United Rugby Championship (URC) Welsh derby of the season by beating Scarlets in Llanelli.

Tries from flanker Dan Thomas, player-of-the-match Taine Basham and replacement hooker Evan Lloyd helped seal the victory, with all three tries coming from effective attacking driving line-outs.

Scarlets scored first-half tries through centre Joe Roberts and full-back Blair Murray but could only manage a second-half penalty from Joe Hawkins.

Wales centre Eddie James starred for Scarlets, but he could not inspire a home victory.

It was a match played in front of a crowd of 7,073 after kicking off at the unfriendly time of quarter to eight on a Saturday evening.

Cardiff, who finished sixth last season and were the only Welsh team to reach the play-offs, were without injured Wales wing Josh Adams but gave debuts to summer signings former Australia prop Scott Sio and Namibia centre Le Roux Malan.

Scarlets, who were 14th in the 2025-26 campaign with only Dragons and Zebre below them, were missing injured number eights Fletcher Anderson and Taine Plumtree, and Wales fly-half Sam Costelow.

Wales props Corey Domachowski and Kemsley Mathias were also absent, as the hosts were led out by vice-captain Ryan Elias, who was making his 200th appearance.

It was the hosts who drew first blood with a superb break from scrum-half Dane Blacker and a neat offload from flanker Sam Lousi releasing Roberts.

Cardiff struck back with a more methodical try as flanker Thomas was driven over from an effective maul.

Scarlets again demonstrated why they looked more dangerous in possession during the first half when Murray scored a fine individual try after being expertly put through a gap by centre James, who showed the deft side in his armoury alongside the power game.

James has been employed as an outside centre by national head coach Steve Tandy but proved against Cardiff why he is a more natural inside centre with his powerful ball-carrying display.

Cardiff defence coach Gethin Jenkins would have been unimpressed by the effortless manner in which Murray glided through the visitors' defence.

Cardiff did not panic, though, and Basham powered over as the visitors led 14-12 at half-time.

In the early second-half exchanges, Murray again showed his threat as a runner, while fly-half Callum Sheedy almost created a chance for Cardiff by cheekily heading the ball after following up his kick.

Sheedy's opposite number Gareth Anscombe had made his competitive debut before he was replaced early in the second half by Joe Hawkins, who made an immediate impression by slotting over a penalty for Scarlets to regain the lead.

Another Wales fly-half, Jarrod Evans, who returned to Cardiff from Harlequins, was introduced among a raft of replacements that included Wales flanker James Botham with the bench proving crucial in the second-half success.

After a lovely sunny day in Llanelli, both sides were treated to driving rain before Scarlets wing Ellis Mee lifted the home crowd by forcing a penalty with an effective tackle and jackal.

Murray's pinpoint kick almost set up an encouraging attacking platform for Scarlets but was deemed to have gone out on the full after hitting the touchline, with referee Adam Jones consulting the television match official (TMO).

This proved a pivotal moment because Cardiff were handed an offensive position and made no mistake with replacement hooker Lloyd diving over.

Evans converted before missing a long-range penalty that would have taken Cardiff two scores clear.

Another James burst gave Scarlets hope before an important turnover from Lloyd stopped the home attack and halted any hopes of a dramatic home revival.

Replacements: McKee, J Morse, Hawley, Groves, T Davies, Hughes, Hawkins, I Jones.

Cardiff: Winnett; Beetham, Malan, B Thomas, Grady; Sheedy, Mulder; Sio, Belcher (capt), Sebastian, McNally, T Williams, Mann, D Thomas, Basham.

Replacements: E Lloyd, Barratt, Wainwright, Thornton, Botham, Bevan, J Evans, Millard.

Assistant referees: Carwyn Sion (WRU), Lloyd Edwards (WRU)

title: Wakefield shock Wigan to reach first Grand Final
description: Wakefield Trinity produce a sensational upset to reach their first ever Super League Grand Final and end Wigan Warriors' hopes of a treble in 2026.
fullText:
Betfred Super League play-off semi-final

Tries: Johnstone 2, Sinfield, Hall, Rodwell Goals: Jowitt 6 Drop-goal: Lino

Wakefield Trinity produced a sensational upset to reach their first ever Super League Grand Final and end Wigan Warriors' hopes of a treble in 2026.

Having led 8-6 at the end of a tight first period, the visitors took full advantage of Adam Keighran's second-half yellow card, with Tom Johnstone, Jack Sinfield and Corey Hall all crossing while the Wigan centre was in the sin-bin.

England winger Johnstone had earlier replied to Brad O'Neill's opener for the Warriors and Ky Rodwell added Wakefield's fifth try as Trinity registered 33 unanswered points to book their spot at Old Trafford.

A Championship side as recently as 2024, Wakefield have made huge progress in recent seasons under ambitious owner Matt Ellis and experienced head coach Daryl Powell - and they are now just one win away from becoming Super League champions.

They will face Warrington Wolves in the title decider on Saturday, 3 October.

Wigan went into the play-off semi-final on a 16-game winning run and with two trophies - the Challenge Cup and the League Leaders' Shield - already secured.

However, their hopes of getting to a fourth consecutive Grand Final were crushed on home soil by an outstanding Wakefield display.

'Pipe dream' to reality? Wakefield reach Grand Final

Relive Wakefield's semi-final win over Wigan

Warrington edge past Leeds to reach Grand Final

Wigan's only points came while Wakefield forward Jezz Tevaga was in the sin-bin for a trip on Liam Marshall, but it was Keighran's yellow card for a late tackle on Isaiah Vagana that proved to be the pivotal moment.

Wakefield's lead stretched from two points to 18 during Keighran's spell off the field, much to the delight of the away supporters stationed behind the end they were attacking.

Mason Lino's drop-goal and Max Jowitt's second penalty of the match added further gloss to the scoreline, and owner Ellis joined the celebrations on the field at full-time.

Only five clubs have won Grand Finals since the first was staged in 1998; Wigan, St Helens, Bradford Bulls, Leeds Rhinos and Hull KR.

Wakefield's win guarantees there will be a sixth name on the trophy and a new champion for the second successive year, following Rovers' victory in 2025.

Warrington have lost all four previous Grand Finals in which they have appeared, the most recent of them in 2018.

Powell, who was in charge of Castleford Tigers when they lost the Grand Final in 2017, is sure to be a central figure in the build-up, given his unspectacular season-and-a-half spell in charge of the Wolves which ended midway through the 2023 campaign.

Meanwhile, try-scoring half-back Sinfield is set to play in a Grand Final 11 years after his father, Sir Kevin Sinfield, made the last of his eight Grand Final appearances.

Sir Kevin won seven titles with Leeds Rhinos and he is scheduled to deliver the match ball before next Saturday's game to round off his latest fundraising effort for motor neurone disease (MND) charities.

"Hopefully he'll be there!" Jack Sinfield told BBC Two. "He's not here tonight because he's starting in the morning, but I'm sure he'll be watching and I can't wait to see him next week.

"I've been there [to Grand Finals] a fair few times watching so it will be nice to do it the other way round and he can hopefully watch me win one."

title: Man City chairman confident club will prove innocence
description: Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak says he is still confident of proving the club's innocence after they were found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules.
fullText:
Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak says he is still confident of proving the club's innocence after they were found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules.

City were accused of a wide range of rule breaches, centring around claims they inflated sponsorship revenue from connected companies and made other "off the books" payments to circumvent financial regulations.

On Friday, it was announced City had been found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 charges brought against them and Al Mubarak has responded with a letter to fans on the club's website.

"Following Friday's media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I," Al Mubarak said.

"Here's what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began.

"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position.

"But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies."

Premier League clubs are seeking legal advice about compensation relating to the charges, while BBC Sport has been told City will appeal.

Sanctions on the club are yet to be announced, but repercussions could include a points deduction, expulsion from the Premier League or a huge fine.

Al Mubarak, who was appointed as City's chairman after their 2008 takeover, also said his club was being "undermined".

"While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed," he added.

"There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club. We will not give them that opportunity."

Man City and the 115 charges - key questions answered

Man City fans face up to reality of guilty verdict

Everton told to pay Burnley £35m over PSR breach

Manchester City vs The Premier League

Meanwhile, Christian Purslow, a former Liverpool managing director and Aston Villa chief executive, who also held a senior role at Chelsea, said the City case could begin a chain of events that would be "appalling for the game".

Speaking on Radio 4's Today programme, Purslow appeared alongside football law expert Paul Gilroy KC, who described the case as a "seismic moment for world football".

Purslow said: "It's a sort of 'where does this end?' because if you look at every single season - the nine seasons which we now know Manchester City breached rules - then all of their 19 Premier League rivals in that season, to differing extents, suffered easy-to-compute loss. Whether it was a place in the Premier League - every place was worth £3m.

"Teams that came fifth who didn't make the Champions League maybe lost tens of millions of pounds - and of course teams that were relegated. Let's say the team that finished 18th would've finished 17th if Manchester City weren't there. And they, of course, suffered huge loss.

"If you add all those claims up, over nine years, and that's just in the Premier League, you can see that the potential here for this to spiral out of control is huge."

Gilroy added that, so far, four clubs have put in protective claims "reserving the right to claim compensation if City are found guilty".

The news, broken by the Athletic,, external came 1,327 days after City were charged by the Premier League in February 2023 following a four-year investigation, and 22 months after a hearing by an independent commission concluded.

No official announcement has been made by the Premier League, which has declined to comment.

Manchester City declined to comment on whether they had been found guilty, instead providing a statement which read: "Premier League process remains ongoing with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has urged the Premier League to come to a quick resolution.

She told BBC Radio 5 Live: "I think most football fans will be feeling that this is not a good moment for football as a whole and I think Manchester City fans will be feeling very, very anxious about what happens next.

"It's very unsettling for football fans and I hope that it can be resolved as swiftly as possible.

"I will obviously look very closely as what comes out of this but we can't apply those rules for the Premier League. They have got to do it themselves and are going to have to resolve this as swiftly as possible - not just for the sake of Manchester City but for the sake of football."

City won eight trophies in the period covered by the case, including three Premier League titles, three EFL Cups, one Community Shield and one FA Cup.

The charges cover the managerial tenures of Roberto Mancini and Manuel Pellegrini, and the first two years under Pep Guardiola, who left the club at the end of last season after 10 years in charge.

David Bernstein, who was Manchester City chairman from 1998-2003, told Times Radio he felt "absolutely awful" on hearing the news of City being found guilty - but admitted any punishment would have to be "more drastic" than a fine.

"To see all this tarnished in this way is very sad," he said.

"I feel particularly bad for the wonderful supporters of the club who've stayed with the club through thick and thin.

"This whole process has taken too long already. So the appeal process now has to be done quickly because you've got the club playing with this cloud over its head and it's just not viable.

"The appeal process cannot go on for year after year, I think that would be a disaster, not just for this particular case but for English football generally. The timing is crucial."

He continued: "I can't give a view on the punishment. If they are found, after the appeal, guilty of 115 charges, my beloved club is going to face a very severe penalty.

"All I would say is that money is not sufficient, it would have to be something, unfortunately, more drastic than that."

Meanwhile, singer-songwriter Noel Gallagher says he is "shocked" at the news and it is "quite sad" for players and fans.

"A little surprised when I heard it on the radio. Surprised because the club have assured us all along that they vehemently denied any of these charges," the Oasis star and City fan said on the Let Me Talk podcast.

"So it was a bit of a shock to find out that we've been found guilty. But really overall just quite sad really. Sad for the fans and for the players."

title: Who made an uncharacteristic error? England player ratings v Spain
description: England were beaten 3-2 in an entertaining game by world champions Spain in the Nations League - here's how BBC Sport rated the Three Lions' players.
fullText:
England were beaten 3-2 in an entertaining game by world champions Spain in the Nations League - the Three Lions' first match since this summer's World Cup.

Lamine Yamal gave Spain the lead before goals from Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane put England ahead.

Kane then missed a penalty before Alex Baena curled in to level the score, with Mikel Oyarzabal scoring the winner.

Here's how we rated England's players - and you can have your say in the comments at the bottom.

James Trafford: Showed early on his ability to play with the ball at his feet but conceded after just two minutes when Guehi gifted the ball to Lamine Yamal. An important save stopped Torres making it 2-0 in the first half. 6

Jarell Quansah: Continued at right-back after showing what he could do in the position at the World Cup. A physically dominant performance and had a chance to score but headed over. 6

Ezri Konsa: Some shaky moments for Konsa and England's back four but the centre-back regrouped and got better as the game went on. 6

Marc Guehi: An uncharacteristic error gifted the ball - and the opening goal - to Lamine Yamal. 5

Nico O'Reilly: Put in the cross for Kane's goal as England took the lead in the first half. Did a good job of trying to deal with Lamine Yamal. However he gave the ball away for Spain's second goal. 6

Elliot Anderson: Nearly punished for giving the ball away in a dangerous position in the first half but Ferran Torres rolled his shot wide. Anderson and midfield partner Lewis-Skelly took some time to settle in what was a tough night in the middle of the pitch against a Spain side who moved the ball so well. 6

Myles Lewis-Skelly: A first England start in centre midfield for Lewis-Skelly after shining for Arsenal. Given the tough task of trying to shut off the supply to Spain's conductor, Rodri. A solid performance. Replaced after 70 minutes. 6

Jude Bellingham: The Real Madrid midfielder produced another dominant display and was unlucky to be on the losing side. He provided an assist for England's equaliser and won a penalty which Kane hit against the bar after slipping. Stung Simon's palms with a drive in stoppage time. 8

Bukayo Saka: Won a couple of free-kicks around the box and shot over from the edge of the area in the first half. Curled just wide with the score level but a quiet night for the winger. 6

Anthony Gordon: The Barcelona winger scored an excellent goal on the counter-attack. He kept calm when played through on goal by Bellingham when his pace put him clear. A dangerous cross in the first half after England went behind and a threat in behind all night. 8

Harry Kane: Started dropping deep in the first half in search of the ball after England went behind. Scored the second with a deflected header to put England in the lead but missed a penalty when they had the chance to add a third in the second half. 7

James Garner (on 70, Lewis-Skelly): Took on Lewis-Skelly's role of trying to keep Rodri quiet. 6

Morgan Rogers (on 70, Gordon): Did not get much of the ball in his 20 minutes on the pitch. 6

Morgan Gibbs-White (on 83, Saka): Came on and played on the left wing. 6

Calvert-Lewin (on 83, Kane): Not much time to impact the play. 6

Jarrad Branthwaite, (on 89, Guehi): A late change for Guehi in the England backline. No time to make an impression. 6

title: Internationals hold three-point lead over US
description: The Internationals team could secure a first President's Cup in 28 years on Sunday after holding off a United States fightback on day three in Medinah.
fullText:
The International team need five points on the final day to secure a first Presidents Cup in 28 years after holding off a United States fightback on day three in Medinah.

The Internationals were behind in every match at one stage but will go into Sunday's singles holding a 10-5-7.5 lead.

The hosts had the better of the morning session, winning two and tying one of the four-balls.

But the teams split the afternoon foursomes, with Canada's Corey Conners saving par at the 18th to win the final match on the course and preserve the Internationals' three-point lead.

The International team have only won the President's Cup once since its inception in 1994 and never on American soil.

"We were down in every match, and to come back and get one and a half points out of this morning, we felt that was a little victory because we were down everywhere," said team captain Geoff Ogilvy.

"This afternoon, the same thing happened. Team USA played so well all day. They played some really high-level foursomes, especially this afternoon.

"For the boys to somehow come back and pinch two points out of that and split the session was amazing."

Sunday sees 12 singles games take place, with each side needing 15.5 points to seal victory.

title: Pickford or Trafford? The battle to be England's number one is now on
description: Jordan Pickford has been England's number one for a long time. But does he now have a rival in James Trafford?
fullText:
You have to go back 10 years to find a major tournament where Jordan Pickford was not starting in goal for England.

The Everton goalkeeper has pretty much been England's number one since making his debut in 2017 - until now.

Saturday's 3-2 Nations League loss to Spain saw Leeds' James Trafford make his competitive debut for the Three Lions as manager Thomas Tuchel signalled the battle to be number one is on.

Pickford became England's highest appearance maker at World Cups, overtaking Peter Shilton when he started in England's 2026 quarter-final win over Norway.

During Gareth Southgate's tenure there was not a natural goalkeeper to rival Pickford, and that looked to continue under Tuchel as Pickford started all but one of England's World Cup qualifiers and then every game in the summer.

But it looks as though Pickford has finally got a rival in Trafford, with Tuchel saying that the pair get "two consecutive matches each" during this international break.

Trafford has impressed since making his move to Leeds for a deal worth up to £45m.

Against Spain, the 23-year-old showed his quality with the ball at his feet and made an impressive save to deny Ferran Torres in the first half.

But he was beaten three times as England lost their Nations League opener to the world champions.

"I think he deserved to get the two matches, that's why we gave him two matches," Tuchel said.

"He started the Premier League season well and gets minutes as number one at Leeds.

"Jordan [Pickford] did absolutely nothing wrong but we wanted to use this competition to see how far actually James is."

Trafford's form this season has helped Leeds to fifth in the Premier League table.

He has kept two clean sheets and now has his chance to stake his claim as England's future number one over two matches.

Trafford had only played 32 top-flight games before moving to Leeds following time at Burnley and Manchester City.

He came through City's academy and joined Burnley for an initial fee of £15m in the summer of 2023.

However, he conceded 67 goals in only 28 matches before losing his place towards the end of the 2023-24 season.

But after starring in Burnley's successful promotion in 2024-25 and the Clarets conceding just 16 goals, Trafford returned to City for £27m last summer with the hope of being Pep Guardiola's number one.

City brought in one of the best goalkeepers in the world in Gianluigi Donnarumma, just four weeks after Trafford's arrival and he became second choice.

Despite it being a frustrating campaign, Trafford did get vital experience and started both the FA Cup final and Carabao Cup final for City before his move to Leeds.

He has been part of England success too, winning the U21 European Championship in 2023 and saving a stoppage-time penalty as Lee Carsley's side beat Spain in the final.

Pickford has kept 46 clean sheets in his 91 appearances for England and has been a huge part of the Three Lions' recent success at major tournaments.

"I think Jordan Pickford will be very disappointed," former England goalkeeper Paul Robinson said on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"Putting myself in that place, he will be questioning why he is not in that place. If he is number one, then why is he not playing against the world champions?

"You wonder whether this is the next generation coming through for Thomas Tuchel."

Pickford put in an excellent performance as England beat Mexico in the World Cup to progress to the quarter-finals, but it was not the goalkeeper's best tournament.

"Jordan Pickford has never let England down," Ian Dennis said.

"You have opposition against the Czech Republic and Croatia where you could give James Trafford an opportunity then. I do find the decision quite strange.

"Pickford against the world champions - you would back him to play in this game."

Pickford is in current possession of the number one shirt and played every minute of the World Cup until he was rested for England's third-place play-off win over France, with Dean Henderson starting.

The 32-year-old, who will be 34 at Euro 2028, has 91 England caps and has saved four of the 14 penalties he has faced in major tournament shootouts.

In the Premier League Pickford's overall numbers dwarf Trafford's. Since the start of the 2024-25 season no-one has prevented more expected goals than the Everton stopper.

But there is very little between the two this campaign with Pickford preventing more goals but Trafford having a higher save percentage and better passing accuracy.

Pickford has been fantastic for England but he didn't have the best World Cup, with a couple conceded that arguably he should've saved and a few nervy moments playing out from the back. Now seems as good a time as any to try James Trafford.

James Trafford deserves to start, he's going to be England's next number one and why not start him against Spain or would you rather he only played against third-rate nations?

James Trafford deserves his shot! Jordan Pickford has been quality for 10 years! Time feels right to test who could be next. Finding the next Harry Kane is going to be the problem!

Jordan Pickford is paying the price for those mistakes creeping in during the World Cup. Could he have stopped the goals v Croatia, DR Congo and Fernandez v Argentina? Prime Pickford does. Thomas Tuchel showing his ruthless side again.

title: Fisher outpoints bloodied Pirotton on Zuffa debut
description: British heavyweight Johnny Fisher wins his first fight under the Zuffa Boxing banner with a majority points victory over Michael Pirotton at the Copper Box Arena.
fullText:
British heavyweight Johnny Fisher won his first fight under the Zuffa Boxing banner with a majority points victory over a bloodied Michael Pirotton at London's Copper Box Arena.

The 27-year-old Essex fighter was the deserved winner in a close bout, but looked laboured at times and appeared to feel the pace over 10 rounds.

Belgian Pirotton, 30, was hampered by a cut around the eye from early in the fight but battled gamely.

He was rocked in the final round as Fisher briefly threatened a stoppage, but Pirotton held on as the judges scored it 95-95, 98-92 and 96-95.

Fisher left the ring shortly after his arm was raised without doing an interview and also did not attend a post-fight interview.

It was Fisher's 15th victory in 16 professional contests on his first appearance since leaving Matchroom Boxing and joining Dana White's Zuffa promotion.

The 7,500-capacity Copper Box was some way short of full, with the upper tier closed and empty seats dotted around the arena.

But Fisher's "Bosh Army" did their best to fill the gaps with noise, giving the "Romford Bull" a raucous reception.

Alongside his social-media star father "Big John", Fisher has built a loyal following through an unusually unfiltered glimpse into family life, training camps and the pair's well-documented enthusiasm for Chinese takeaways.

Fisher started with intent, swinging heavy hooks and reddening Pirotton's eye in the opening round.

The little-known Belgian was unfazed by the home support or Fisher's pressure, but his eye was cut by the second.

"I can see, don't stop the fight," Pirotton told the referee before a doctor examined him in the fourth.

Allowed to continue, he came out firing, but Fisher responded with a flurry to head and body.

Blood stained Pirotton's white shorts, yet he rallied in the fifth - his best round - as Fisher began to look tired and static.

Among those in attendance were British fighters Derek Chisora, Conor Benn and Caroline Dubois, alongside WWE stars AJ Styles and LA Knight.

WWE is owned by American sports and entertainment group TKO, which is also behind Zuffa Boxing.

The doctor took another look at Pirotton before the seventh but allowed the bout to continue.

Neither man was offering much by the latter stages until a short right hand from Fisher staggered Pirotton in the 10th.

For a moment, a 13th stoppage victory appeared within reach, but Fisher could not find the finishing burst as Pirotton slipped to his third loss in 15 fights.

The Copper Box Arena has already become a fitting stage for the contrasting fortunes of Fisher's career. In July 2024, he overwhelmed Alen Babic in just 36 seconds, producing his most explosive victory to date.

Ten months later, in the same ring, he was comprehensively stopped in five rounds by Doncaster's Dave Allen.

Keen to put that behind him, Fisher got the victory he needed on Saturday - if not quite the emphatic performance he might have wanted.

Fisher has repeatedly insisted he wants to be known as more than a popular ticket-seller with a catchy nickname and viral antics.

His profile has raced ahead of his achievements in the ring, and the two meetings with Allen offered the clearest indication yet of the gap he must close if his British-title ambitions are to become reality.

Current British heavyweight champion Richard Riakporhe has already offered Fisher a shot at the belt. The former cruiserweight world champion would represent a considerable jump in level and a far sterner examination than Pirotton.

Former world champion Deontay Wilder has also been mooted as an opponent, but a meeting with former world-title challenger Dillian Whyte appears the more realistic possibility, with Fisher saying there is a "good chance" that contest could come next.
